Independent investigator Roscoe Clark told Fox News that he is certain that Hoffa is buried in an undisclosed location in Michigan, and that it would take less than five minutes.

"Forensics will help solve the Jimmy Hoffa cold case," Clark said. "A team of experts is ready to move forward because of a lack of action by law enforcement. A location has been identified within three feet," and he said the necessary locating equipment is ready to be deployed.

The FBI said it has "received countless tips and information from the public, which have been a tremendous help to the FBI. We are grateful to the public, and most importantly, for the Hoffa's family assistance and support over the years."

UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH STUDENTS SAY SUDIKSHA KONANKI'S 'CRAZY' DISAPPEARANCE COULD 'HAPPEN TO ANYBODY'

Observers note that the legacy of Jimmy Hoffa is not what happened to him, but what he accomplished. His hard-fought victories at the bargaining table and on the picket lines enabled generations to enjoy the American Dream, with healthcare and benefits, good pay and retirement. Millions of sons and daughters and their families still benefit from the feisty labor leader's achievements. In some ways, that is how Jimmy Hoffa is still with us, even as he is still deeply missed and mourned by his family.

James Hoffa, his sister Barbara, their adult children and grandchildren somberly mark this day with each passing year.

Every July 30 "is a hard day," said James Hoffa. "We always spend time with it. It is special time, a time to remember. The good thing is, that I had a great father and he did a great job in raising our family. He was a great man and we miss him."

The in-depth series "Riddle, The Search for James R. Hoffa," is streaming on Fox Nation.

Eric Shawn, a New York-based anchor and senior correspondent for FOX News Channel (FNC), joined the network when it launched in 1996. He is currently the co-anchor of FOX News Live. Shawn is also the host of Riddle: The Search for James R. Hoffa on FOX Nation, FNC's on-demand subscription-based streaming service, which is based upon his extensive reporting into the appearance of notorious Teamsters boss Jimmy Hoffa.

articles.title: WNBA admits controversial betting video featuring Angel Reese, Paige Bueckers 'missed the mark'
articles.excerpt: A Seattle Storm co-owner was suspended after allegedly cursing at teenage fans who supported Sophie Cunningham's stance on women's sports. Former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines discusses the incident, emph...
articles.body_text:
A Seattle Storm co-owner was suspended after allegedly cursing at teenage fans who supported Sophie Cunningham's stance on women's sports. Former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines discusses the incident, emphasizing the importance of fair and safe opportunities for biological girls in sports. The Seattle Storm later apologized, stating their commitment to an inclusive environment.

The WNBA doesn't appear to be taking what could be a direct violation of its own anti-gambling policy very seriously whatsoever.

Ahead of Wednesday night's matchup between the Dallas Wings and Atlanta Dream, the WNBA's official X account shared a video showing Dallas' Paige Bueckers and Atlanta's Angel Reese – two of the league's most well-known players – making a $400 wager on the game. The WNBA was quick to delete the post, but not before many were able to share and also capture recordings of the video.

A WNBA spokesperson released a statement on Thursday claiming that the quickly deleted video was "intended to be lighthearted," but that it "simply missed the mark."

Paige Bueckers #5 of the Dallas Wings and Angel Reese #5 of the Chicago Sky react during the 2025 AT&T WNBA All-Star practice sessions at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on July 18, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images)

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

"While the social media post was intended to be lighthearted, WNBA players are well aware of the league's policies prohibiting betting on WNBA games and receive training every year reinforcing those policies," the statement read.

"We recognized that the post missed the mark, removed it shortly after it was published, and addressed the matter internally. We will also use this as an opportunity to reemphasize with the players involved that conversations about wagering on WNBA games, even when intended as a joke, can have negative consequences."

It is unclear whether the statement's note that the matter was handled "internally" is in reference to the league having conversations with Reese and Bueckers about the clip or the individual who originally shared the video across the league's official social media. OutKick contacted the league for further clarification but did not immediately hear back.

Paige Bueckers #5 of the Dallas Wings plays defense on Angel Reese #5 of the Atlanta Dream on May 22, 2026 at Gateway Center Arena at College Park in Atlanta, Georgia. (Joe Boatman/NBAE via Getty Images)

When reached for comment about the video and any potential in-house investigations regarding the video, a Dream spokesperson told OutKick that the team has "no additional information to share other than what the league released." The Wings were not reached for comment.

Following Atlanta's 82-81 win on Wednesday, a laughing Reese joked that she would be requesting Bueckers' Apple Pay to receive her winnings from the wager.

Betting of any kind is strictly prohibited under the WNBA's new collective bargaining agreement, with Section 5 of Article 14 in the agreement dedicated to gambling regulations.

"Any player found by the Commissioner after a hearing to have been guilty of wagering (directly or indirectly), or of offering or attempting to wager, money or anything of value on the outcome, score, or any other aspect of any WNBA Competition shall, in the sole discretion of the Commissioner, be subject to a fine, suspension, and/or dismissal and disqualification from any further association with the WNBA," subsection c in the agreement reads.

While the WNBA described the wager between Bueckers and Reese as being "lighthearted," it was still a bet made between two players, caught on video, and shared across social media. One would think that WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert has the evidence to potentially impose punishments.

Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese of the USA during the Women's World Cup 2026 Qualifying Tournament Content Day on March 10, 2026, in San Juan, Puerto Rico. (Alexa Alejandro/FIBA via Getty Images)

Other professional sports leagues have strict anti-gambling policies in place that carry severe punishments.

NFL players are prohibited from placing any wagers on NFL games. An NFL player wagering on an NFL game that does not involve his team carries an indefinite suspension of 1-year minimum, while wagering on your own team results in an indefinite two-year suspension.

In the MLB, if a player is found to be betting on games not involving their own team, the player is handed a one-year suspension. If found to be betting on games involving their own team, a lifetime ban is enforced under Major League Rule 21.

OutKick's Alejandro Avila contributed to this report.

articles.title: F1 boss invokes George Lucas while talking about how the series can appeal to new fans
articles.excerpt: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert continues to face intense scrutiny for her leadership missteps, especially surrounding Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark. But despite mounting criticism, some in ...
articles.body_text:
WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert continues to face intense scrutiny for her leadership missteps, especially surrounding Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark. But despite mounting criticism, some in the media are rushing to shield her.

I'm a massive fan of George Lucas as a person. I grew up with the Star Wars prequels, and I like that, despite being a gazillionaire, he's still rocking the same flannels he always has.

The legendary filmmaker — fresh off a great cameo in the movie "Minions and Monsters" — is a big racing fan, and is often seen at Formula 1 races.

He also binned a Scion during the old Toyota Pro/Celebrity Race at Long Beach in one of my favorite videos ever.

George Lucas visited the Ferrari garage at this past weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix. (Photo by Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto)

So he knows racing — hell, he invented podracing — but F1 president and CEO Stefano Domenicali revealed a wild bit of advice he got from the man who somehow invented both Darth Vader and Jar-Jar Binks: no one is interested in how F1 cars are driven.

I don't think that's true, but let's hear him out.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The series has faced a lot of flak for its current cars that rely more heavily on battery power and have effectively changed how drivers have to drive. Certain iconic corners are no longer taken flat out, and the need to recharge batteries has led to people calling the racing artificial.

It has also led to claims that F1 should offer more info about the batteries and their state of charge for fans to follow along.

F1 president and CEO Stefano Domenicali addressed what he — and George Lucas — believe fans are looking for when it comes to the sport. (Photo by Marcel van Dorst/EYE4IMAGES/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"I think that the truth is exactly the other way around, because no one is interested in how you drive your car," Domenicali said, per Motorsport. "The people are interested in whether you are overtaking or not. That's the vast majority of people."

He noted that while some people are interested in this sort of thing, casual fans aren't.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Then he delivered one of the greatest name drops I've ever read.

"I had an interesting discussion with George Lucas in Hungary, and he was giving me an incredible view on how the new fans are watching F1," Domenicali said. "And I think that he gave us an incredible clearance to see how we can really simplify things because the new fans are not understanding the truth, what is behind the scenes."

I think new fans appreciate the sport more once they get a firmer grasp on the behind-the-scenes stuff, but it's interesting Lucas made this point because it sounds to me like he's saying what's most important is providing an entertaining product.

He knows quite a bit about that. Hell, he just opened a massive museum devoted to the medium of storytelling.

George Lucas has a long history with F1, including the 2005 Monaco Grand Prix in which Red Bull ran a livery promoting "Star Wars: Episode III: Revenge of the Sith." (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images)

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

And, if you think about it, every race is one big story, and it makes sense that F1 would want that at the forefront for newer fans.

But, if you're already in the door, there's always room to nerd out on the strategies and tech and science behind the sport, just like if you're a fan of a movie, you can geek out on the plot devices and the structure and even what pen or script software the person who wrote it used.

It's an interesting thing to think about... and even more fun because it seems to have sprung from the flannel-shirted mind of one George Lucas.

articles.title: 10-year-old boy's body pulled from New Jersey river as rescuers search for his sister
articles.excerpt:
Rescuers in New Jersey search for a 10-year-old girl in the Passaic River. The body of the girl's 10-year-old brother was already found. (Credit: WNYW)

Rescuers in New Jersey are still searching for ...
articles.body_text:
Rescuers in New Jersey search for a 10-year-old girl in the Passaic River. The body of the girl's 10-year-old brother was already found. (Credit: WNYW)

Rescuers in New Jersey are still searching for a 10-year-old girl after finding her 10-year-old brother's body in the Passaic River late Wednesday night, Passaic Mayor Hector Lora told reporters.

'Right now, all of our efforts are in trying to recover the body but hoping that perhaps, maybe hope against all things, that we could find the little girl still alive," Lora told FOX 5 New York in an interview.

Lora hoped aloud that the little girl was still alive, hypothesizing that her now deceased brother helped push her to safety.

‘HERO' MOM DIES AFTER USING LAST STRENGTH TO SAVE 4-YEAR-OLD SON FROM FLORIDA RIVER

Passaic Police and other assisting towns work the scene where a 10-year-old boy was found dead, and an ongoing operation is underway to find a 10-year-old girl after both children were in the Passaic River in the vicinity of Veterans Ct near a park in Passaic, New Jersey, on Wednesday, July 29, 2026.  (Kyle Mazza/Sipa USA)

"The 10-year-old boy, as he was going down, maybe an angel, maybe God used him to push his little sister, and now she made her way out so she's home. But the mother has lost her little boy," Lora said.

Lora also told reporters that calls for help came in around 6:20 p.m. local time Wednesday after bystanders saw three children in the water, according to FOX 5.

A good Samaritan unsuccessfully tried to help the children out of the water, the outlet reported.

Passaic Police and other assisting towns work the scene inside the Passaic River where a 10-year-old boy was found dead and an ongoing operation is underway to recover a 10-year-old girl after both children were in the Passaic River in the vicinity of Veterans Ct near a park in Passaic, New Jersey,  (Kyle Mazza/Sipa USA)

PARK VISITORS FACE FLOOD DANGER OUT WEST WHILE SEVERE STORMS RIP THROUGH NY, NJ

Search and rescue operations were ongoing into Thursday morning. The efforts were hampered in part by high water levels due to recent storms.

The search and rescue operations included members of the the Passaic Police Department, the Passaic County Sheriff's Office and the New Jersey State Police.

Passaic Police and other assisting towns work the scene inside the Passaic River after two children were swept into the Passaic River in the vicinity of Veterans Ct near a park in Passaic, New Jersey, on Thursday, July 30, 2026. A (Kyle Mazza/Sipa USA)

Fox News Digital contacted the Passaic Police Department, the Passaic County Sheriff's Office and the New Jersey State Police for further information.

articles.title: Bodycam shows Los Angeles County deputy stabbed seconds after arriving at knife attack
articles.excerpt:
Deputies responded to reports of a man armed with multiple knives when the suspect suddenly charged an arriving deputy. (Credit: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

Newly released body camera an...
articles.body_text:
Deputies responded to reports of a man armed with multiple knives when the suspect suddenly charged an arriving deputy. (Credit: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

Newly released body camera and surveillance footage shows a Los Angeles County sheriff's deputy being stabbed within seconds of arriving at a call about an armed man before deputies opened fire, fatally shooting the suspect.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department on Tuesday released body camera and surveillance video from the June 20 incident in a Lancaster parking lot that left a deputy wounded and 23-year-old Robert Castro shot. Castro died after the shooting.

The incident began with a 911 caller reporting a man wielding multiple knives in public.

WISCONSIN PROTESTER BRANDS MADISON AS 'CORRUPT CITY' DURING ANTI-POLICE TIRADE FOLLOWING DEADLY SHOOTING

"Hey, I just want to make a report of a guy with some knives ... swinging them in public," the caller told a dispatcher.

Body camera footage released by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department shows 23-year-old Robert Castro moments before authorities say he stabbed a sheriff's deputy during a June 20 encounter in Lancaster, California. (Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

The caller said Castro appeared to be "fighting with someone" while carrying a large knife and expressed concern after seeing him look toward a woman walking to a nearby bus stop.

Surveillance video shows deputies arriving with emergency lights activated as Castro walked across the parking lot while still armed.

VIDEO SHOWS UNDERCOVER COPS SHOOTING MAN THREATENING SHOPPERS WITH FAKE GUN IN ‘JUSTIFIED’ DEFENSE: OFFICIALS

According to the sheriff's department, Castro suddenly changed direction before the first deputy's patrol vehicle had come to a stop, rushed toward the deputy, pulled a knife and stabbed him.

A still image from deputy body camera footage released by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department shows Robert Castro approaching an arriving deputy while holding what investigators say was one of three knives recovered at the scene. (Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

The wounded deputy then drew his service weapon and opened fire.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

The deputy activated his body camera after firing his weapon, but the camera's pre-event recording feature captured the 60 seconds leading up to the stabbing without audio.

EIGHT NYPD OFFICERS INJURED IN MASSIVE EXPLOSION WHILE RESPONDING TO KNIFE-WIELDING MAN IN QUEENS HOME

A second deputy's body camera captured him arriving as the first deputy fired his weapon.

Surveillance video released by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department shows deputies arriving at the scene before investigators say Robert Castro suddenly charged toward an arriving deputy and stabbed him. (Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

The video shows Castro on the ground as the deputy checked on his wounded colleague. When Castro moved one of his hands, the deputy repeatedly yelled, "Stop reaching," before opening fire again.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department released images of two knives recovered after authorities say 23-year-old Robert Castro stabbed a sheriff's deputy during a June 20 confrontation in Lancaster, California. (Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

Deputies rendered medical aid to Castro until Los Angeles County Fire Department personnel arrived. Castro was transported to a hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.

Authorities said Castro was armed with three knives, including the one investigators say he used to stab the deputy.

The wounded deputy was hospitalized for treatment. No other deputies or civilians were injured.

The California Department of Justice is investigating the shooting, as required under state law for officer-involved fatalities.

The sheriff's department said it released the video before the investigation was complete "in the interest of transparency with the community we serve."

Greg Wehner is a reporter for Fox News Digital covering U.S. news and crime, with a focus on breaking developments, law enforcement, public safety and major stories shaping communities across the country.

articles.title: Older adults taking 5 or more prescription drugs face higher risk of death, study finds
articles.excerpt: Older adults who walked at a significantly faster speed than their peers were about half as likely to develop cognitive impairment, according to Dr. Joe Verghese, MD, neurologist at Stony Brook Medici...
articles.body_text:
Older adults who walked at a significantly faster speed than their peers were about half as likely to develop cognitive impairment, according to Dr. Joe Verghese, MD, neurologist at Stony Brook Medicine.

Older adults who take five or more prescription medications face a significantly higher risk of death compared to those taking fewer drugs, according to a study published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society.

The research highlights the growing concern over polypharmacy, the medical term for taking five or more daily prescriptions, and its long-term effects on aging populations.

Led by Dr. Alexander Chaitoff of the University of Michigan School of Medicine, researchers analyzed national survey data collected from 7,828 adults aged 65 and older between 1999 and 2016.

LONGER LIVES, WORSE HEALTH? SCIENTISTS UNCOVER TROUBLING TREND ACROSS GENERATIONS

Trained staff directly inspected participants' pill bottles to verify medication use over the previous 30 days, then followed them for an average of 8.5 years, according to a press release.

More than half of participants (54.3%) fell into at least one high-risk medication category. The largest group consisted of older adults taking five or more prescription drugs (polypharmacy).

Over 40% of older adults studied were taking five or more prescription medications, a situation known as polypharmacy. (iStock)

Another group, 37.6% of those studied, used medications deemed risky for older individuals, such as drugs that can increase the risk of confusion or falls, the study revealed.

DOCTORS REVEAL HIDDEN DANGER FOR SOME OZEMPIC, WEGOVY USERS WITH BRAIN DISORDERS

Additionally, 11.4% took combinations of medications that are known to cause major drug-to-drug interactions.

After accounting for overall health and underlying conditions, taking five or more prescriptions was associated with a 38% increase in overall mortality risk. Each additional prescription medication added to a patient’s routine was linked to a 7% increase in death risk.

Taking multiple medications has been shown to increase the likelihood of side effects, adverse drug reactions and accidental overdose, particularly as the liver and kidneys age and process drugs less efficiently, according to medical experts at Cleveland Clinic.

Researchers emphasized that these findings can help doctors identify patients who would benefit from safely stopping or reducing unnecessary medications. (iStock)

The total number of medications participants took was the strongest independent predictor of mortality, even after accounting for drug-to-drug interactions and potentially inappropriate prescriptions.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

These findings could help doctors determine which patients are the best candidates for "deprescribing," or carefully reducing or stopping unnecessary medications, the researchers stated.

The authors noted several limitations, including that the study focused strictly on community-dwelling older adults, excluding those living in nursing homes or assisted care facilities.

Because the study relied on a single 30-day snapshot of medication use, it shows an association rather than direct proof that the prescriptions caused the higher death risk. (iStock)

Additionally, medication use was documented during a single 30-day snapshot at the start of the study, meaning researchers could not track subsequent changes in prescriptions or evolving health conditions over time.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Experts emphasized that observational studies show association rather than direct causation. Older adults taking higher numbers of prescriptions often suffer from multiple severe or complex health conditions, which independently carry a higher mortality risk.

Khloe Quill is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital. She and the lifestyle team cover a range of story topics including food and drink, travel, and health.

articles.title: Savannah Bananas stars trade baseball dreams for kids' smiles: 'Exactly where God put me'
articles.excerpt:
Members of the Savannah Bananas didn't have this type of fame on their bingo card, but they have no complaints after surprising children at a hospital.

Reese Alexiades and DR Meadows had baseball dre...
articles.body_text:
Members of the Savannah Bananas didn't have this type of fame on their bingo card, but they have no complaints after surprising children at a hospital.

Reese Alexiades and DR Meadows had baseball dreams just like the rest of us – getting to the major leagues. But their journeys took them on a route unimaginable even less than five years ago.

Alexiades played college ball at Pepperdine University, while Meadows played for Division II school Columbus State. Neither played minor league ball, but they now play in front of one of the largest baseball crowds ever.

Alexiades and Meadows hit the big time in another way, becoming stars for the Savannah Bananas. Meadows is the organization's all-time leader in "trick plays," while Alexiades plays with a cape on.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Savannah Bananas Reese Alexiades and DR Meadows meet with children at a children's hospital with Dairy Queen. (Dairy Queen)

Despite selling out MLB ballparks and even playing in front of six-figure crowds at football stadiums, baseball purists will never get on board – unless, Alexiades says, "if they came to a game and caught an out." (If a fan catches a ball on the fly, the batter is out.)

But what fans do not understand the most, Meadows says, is that, contrary to popular belief, their games are not "scripted" like, say, the Harlem Globetrotters.

"There's a huge difference. In our league, all our teams are out to win. We're very competitive... Just this past weekend, we lost two out of three in Chicago against the Firefighters, and our guys were not happy," Meadows told Fox News Digital in a recent interview. "At the end of the day, we're there for a bigger picture: to put on a show for the fans, break down the wall for the kids there and put smiles on faces. That's what makes Banana Ball beautiful. Even though we get to have fun competing, winning and losing, we still get to make somebody's day."

No one Meadows and Alexiades' age grew up wanting to be Bananas – but that may have changed by now.

"One of the big reasons why I fell in love with baseball is looking up to other players. Now kids can look up to us, and what we're all about is bringing fun to the game of baseball. Kids being able to see us and see how much fun we have, that's what it's all about. We try to be the best role models we can be for kids because the kids are what it's all about," Alexiades said.

Meadows added, "You see kids at the Little League World Series listing their favorite players, and some are Bananas players. To know we have that kind of platform — and like Reese was saying, it all comes from having fun, playing the game and having fun. Youth sports these days should be less pressure and a lot more fun. I think it's cool that kids are getting to see how much fun we have and get to take that to their own game."

The Savannah Bananas' mascot Split dances atop the first-base dugout. (Ben McCanna/Portland Press Herald via Getty Images)

FORMER SAVANNAH BANANAS PLAYER NAMED MLB ALL-STAR, HOURS AFTER HITTING FOR CYCLE AS A ROOKIE

Alexiades and Meadows recently visited a children's hospital in Tennessee to give them some Dairy Queen, and on Thursday, for every Blizzard bought at select locations, at least $1 will be donated to Children’s Miracle Network to help support local children’s hospitals.

"That's the beauty of our platform and this partnership: We can really make an impact, and so can other people," Alexiades said.

"Getting to see those kids, put a smile on their faces, bring them Blizzard Treats and enjoy those with them was super cool. The amount of joy DQ brings and the Bananas bring – it all made sense," added Meadows.

So, while it may not be the big time they originally envisioned, it's the 2026 version of the big time, which is just fine with the baseball player in a cape – literally and figuratively.

Members of the Savannah Bananas attend a children's hospital with Dairy Queen. (Dairy Queen)

"The whole goal is to be able to play the game we love for as long as we can. A lot of us, me included, and people in this organization have been told no at some point in their careers. The Bananas have given me a chance to keep going, keep playing and realize that it's for a bigger purpose now," Alexiades said.

"I get to go and probably have more fun than I would have ever had if I played in the major leagues. So I'm having the time of my life, and this is exactly where God put me."

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X, and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

articles.title: White House blasts Spanish government as thousands of migrants surge from Morocco, emergency request denied
articles.excerpt:

The White House bashed Spain's left-wing government af...
articles.body_text:
Thousands of migrants from Morocco pored over the country's border with Spain and into Spain's African enclave of Ceuta July 30, 2026. (Reuters)

The White House bashed Spain's left-wing government after the border between Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta and Morocco collapsed Thursday.

"President Trump has long warned Europe what would happen if they continue to implement far-left, globalist policies, including enabling mass migration," White House principal deputy press secretary Anna Kelly told Fox News in a statement.

"Spain and other countries who have adopted this destructive philosophy should immediately reverse course or risk their own demise."

TRUMP CRITICIZES SPAIN AMID IRAN, NATO RIFT AS PM SANCHEZ FACES QUESTIONS OVER POLITICAL MOTIVES

Ceuta's president formally requested a national emergency declaration Thursday after more than 2,000 migrants crossed the border from Morocco in the past 10 days. Videos showed chaotic scenes of migrants pouring into the Spanish territory.

Video shows hordes of apparently military-aged men smiling and posing for cameras, some carrying swimming flippers, and sprinting through the streets as authorities struggle to corral the unruly masses.

Migrants run and cheer as they cross on foot into the North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco after swimming over from the Moroccan side and overwhelming police at the city's breakwater, according to Spain's Guardia Civil, in Ceuta, Spain, July 30, 2026. (Faro TV via Reuters)

Other footage shows crowds of migrants emerging from the sea, climbing up onto Ceuta's rocky shores and working their way around border fences.

Ceuta President Juan Jesús Vivas formally requested that Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declare a national emergency to help respond to the border crisis, Spanish media outlets reported. Madrid, however, denied the request.

DEM REP SETH MOULTON SAYS PARTY HAS NO IMMIGRATION PLAN, IS ONLY ‘OPPOSITION TO TRUMP’

"The declaration of a national emergency is part of the state civil protection regulations, which do not consider migratory flows as a risk to the National Civil Protection System, nor do they establish special plans, basic guidelines, or specific civil protection instruments for their management. Therefore, it is not possible to activate this mechanism, as requested by the president of the Government of Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas," Spain's Ministry of the Interior said in a statement, according to Spanish outlet El País.

Ceuta’s government, in its request for a national emergency declaration, noted that immigration from Morocco is always a problem for the Spanish enclave but claimed the last 10 days represented a peak "of particular intensity." That peak has seen more than 2,000 migrants cross the border in the past 10 days, Ceuta officials said, according to El País.

Spanish and Moroccan maritime patrols, supported by Spain's Maritime Rescue service, conduct rescue operations off the southern coast of Ceuta after a sharp increase in migrant arrivals to the Spanish enclave in North Africa. (Antonio Sempere/JNA Press/Sipa USA)

"The Government of Spain is fully committed to providing an immediate response to the situation in Ceuta. We are mobilizing all necessary resources, working with Moroccan and international authorities, and preparing the necessary measures to restore normalcy as soon as possible," Sánchez wrote in a Thursday post on X.

BIDEN ADMINISTRATION FORCED A FALSE CHOICE ON AMERICANS ABOUT IMMIGRATION

Sánchez has faced considerable backlash from his country's conservatives for his policies on immigration, with many arguing that Spain's policy of guaranteeing social services to minors who illegally enter the country incentivizes mass migration.

Migrants cross on foot into the North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco by attempting to swim, according to Spain's Guardia Civil, near the border with Ceuta, in Fnideq, Morocco, July 30, 2026, in a still image obtained by Reuters (Reuters)

"When they cross the border as minors, you cannot send them back to Morocco," Javier Negre, a conservative Spanish journalist and owner of La Derecha Diario and UHN Plus, told Fox News Digital.

"The Spanish state has to take care of them and pay money to NGOs to care for these minors until they turn 18," Negre continued.

"It’s proof that Europe and Spain are on the verge of becoming a failed continent because of the future policies and promotion of this illegal invasion under Pedro Sánchez."

Sánchez, for his part, has claimed that accepting migrants is necessary to keep Spain's economy alive, arguing the country's low birth rates necessitate accepting immigrants.

Spain's Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, delivers a statement at the Moncloa Palace in Madrid, Spain. (AP Photo/Andrea Comas)

"The West needs people. Currently, few of its countries have a rising population growth rate," Sánchez wrote in a February op-ed in The New York Times.

"Unless they embrace migration, they will experience a sharp demographic decline that will prevent them from keeping their economies and public services afloat. Their gross domestic product will stagnate. Their public healthcare and pension systems will suffer.

"Neither AI nor robots will be able to prevent this outcome. ... The only option to avoid decline is to integrate migrants in the most orderly and effective way possible."

Fox News Digital contacted the offices of Sánchez and Vivas for further comment.

Fox News' Patrick Ward contributed to this report.

articles.title: Ex-White House counsel says Epstein accuser’s testimony ‘lacked inherent credibility’
articles.excerpt:
Kathryn Ruemmler was blasted by family of late Virginia Giuffre after House committee transcripts were released

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A former White House counsel and for...
articles.body_text:
Kathryn Ruemmler was blasted by family of late Virginia Giuffre after House committee transcripts were released

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A former White House counsel and former general counsel of Goldman Sachs, who has faced scrutiny over her past ties to Jeffrey Epstein, told a House committee this month that some of the allegations made by one his most prominent accusers “lacked inherent credibility”, according to newly released transcripts.

Kathryn Ruemmler’s name appeared thousands of times in records related to Epstein, the disgraced financier and convicted sex offender, that were released earlier this year by the US Department of Justice under the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

The files revealed Ruemmler had accepted gifts from Epstein, who died by suicide while awaiting trial in 2019 after he was arrested by federal authorities, at times addressed him as “Uncle Jeffrey” and “sweetie” in emails, and offered him informal advice on how to respond to questions about his sex crimes.

Ruemmler’s testimony before Congress when she was asked about Virginia Giuffre, a victim of Epstein’s abuse, was swiftly criticized by Giuffre’s family. “She should be ashamed of herself,” Giuffre’s brother and sister-in-law, Sky and Amanda Roberts, told CNN. Giuffre died by suicide in April 2025.

“Do you believe that Virginia Giuffre was a victim of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell?” the House oversight committee asked Ruemmler, who served as the White House counsel in the Obama administration, during her interview with the panel earlier this month part of its investigation into Epstein.

“I don’t know,” she responded, according to a transcript released on Wednesday.

Ruemmler went on to add: “If she says that she was, I don’t have a reason to doubt that. However, there were allegations that she made that were, I believed based on my experience as a former prosecutor and as a defense counsel, that were of such a nature that they were – they lacked inherent credibility.

“Typically, when someone says, I was sex trafficked to someone, they say who, when, where, not multiple world leaders, multiple foreign presidents,” she said.

Her remarks were condemned by Giuffre’s brother and sister-in-law, Sky and Amanda Roberts, who said in a statement to CNN that it as “reprehensible” to “attempt to cast doubt on Virginia, whose bravery was the reason so many other survivors stepped forward, resulting in more than 50 people having to step down from their positions of power”.

They said that “the only person who lacks credibility is Kathy Ruemmler”.

Giuffre, one of Epstein’s most prominent accusers, had previously testified and alleged that Epstein and Maxwell had abused her as a teenager, and trafficked her to powerful men, including Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, who has repeatedly denied the allegations against him.

Jennifer Connelly, a spokesperson for Ruemmler, said in a statement: “As Ms Ruemmler told the committee, she had no knowledge of any ongoing criminal activity by Epstein and there is not a shred of evidence to suggest otherwise.”

“Ms Ruemmler would never turn a blind eye to any criminal activity and if she had seen or heard anything to suggest that Epstein was harming women or girls, she would have taken action to stop it,” she added.

Another representative for Ruemmler also told CNN in a statement – before Giuffre’s family members had issued their statement – that Ruemmler “was responding to a specific discussion about specific allegations” and was “expressing skepticism regarding particular claims that had not been substantiated, not every allegation Ms Giuffre ever made”.

The transcript was released about two weeks after Ruemmler appeared before the committee. She was called to testify after the Epstein files revealed dozens of emails between her and Epstein between 2014 and 2019. At one point she had been listed as a backup executor of his will, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Ruemmler told lawmakers during the interview that they had a professional relationship and that Epstein had “used” her “to legitimize his standing” and that “it was a mistake to deal with” him.

She insisted that she never saw any “evidence of ongoing criminal conduct or misconduct of any kind by Epstein during the time I dealt with him” and also told lawmakers that “many” of her emails with Epstein had been “taken out of context or do not mean what some have speculated or suggested”.

Ruemmler announced in February that she would be resigning from her role at Goldman Sachs as chief legal officer.

articles.title: Eagles coach Vic Fangio mocks Anthony Fauci's Senate hearing spectacle during his own press conference
articles.excerpt: Dr. Anthony Fauci pleaded the Fifth Amendment 111 times in a Senate hearing regarding COVID-19 origins. Sen. Rand Paul, chairman of the Senate Homeland Security Committee, is pushing to hold Fauci in ...
articles.body_text:
Dr. Anthony Fauci pleaded the Fifth Amendment 111 times in a Senate hearing regarding COVID-19 origins. Sen. Rand Paul, chairman of the Senate Homeland Security Committee, is pushing to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress, noting Fauci's own diary entry from January 2020 indicated the wet market was an amplifier, not the source, of the virus.

The start of any NFL training camp is a life-consuming experience that leaves participants with little time for anything else, but Philadelphia Eagles coach Vic Fangio showed Thursday he can still keep up with other things: Like Anthony Fauci's Senate hearing.

The defensive coordinator got in front of reporters for a regularly scheduled news conference and promptly fielded the first question that, if you know Philly reporters, wasn't a softball.

"I'm going to be like Fauci and just take the Fifth Amendment on your question," Fangio said. "Did you guys see that?

Dec 1, 2024; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Philadelphia Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio on the field before the game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. (Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images)

TOP 5 MOMENTS FROM FAUCI'S HEARING: PAUL BOOTS LAWYER, MORENO ERUPTS AS CONTEMPT VOTE LOOMS

He watched segments of the hearings in which the former Director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) and a cornerstone member of the White House Coronavirus Task Force during the Covid-19 pandemic testified before senators.

Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment so as to not incriminate himself more than 100 times – 111 times by some counts.

Fauci, 85, was subpoenaed to appear before the Senate’s government oversight committee by Chairman Rand Paul (R-Kentucky), who has alleged Fauci should be jailed for covering up the origins of the Covid-19 pandemic and even helped cause the pandemic by funding Coronavirus research in Wuhan, China, where the outbreak began in 2019.

RAND PAUL SEEKS CONTEMPT CHARGES AFTER FAUCI INVOKES FIFTH AMENDMENT MORE THAN 100 TIMES

Dr. Anthony Fauci is sworn in during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs committee hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC, on July 29, 2026. Dr. Fauci, the former Director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, is testifying after Senator Rand Paul, Republican from Kentucky, released more than 1000 pages of Fauci's diary entries from the COVID-19 pandemic. (Alex Wroblewski / AFP via Getty Images)

Fauci refused to answer the most mundane questions despite the fact that President Joe Biden gave him a full, unconditional and preemptive pardon.

The good doctor wouldn't even answer questions about the color of his tie or the carpet.

And Fangio, who attended the Eagles' Super Bowl celebration at the White House in 2025, was not impressed.

(One supposes he's like a lot of Americans who want answers because, like everything else, the NFL was deeply affected by the Covid-19 pandemic).

Fangio, 67, did not watch the entire Fauci circus act, according to a source. He was, however, interested in the highlights and takeaways from the session.

President Donald Trump greets Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley at a White House event welcoming the 2025 Super Bowl champion Eagles on the South Lawn in Washington, D.C., on April 28, 2025. Trump honored the Eagles after their second Super Bowl victory. (Getty Images)

Later, during his nearly 12-minute news conference, Fangio was asked a question that Eagles' executive vice president and general manager Howie Roseman was asked the day before.

Fangio noted Roseman was asked the same question but didn't know what Roseman offered as an answer.

"He ducked you?" Fangio asked the reporter. "He Fauci-ed you?"

We know how Vic Fangio feels about Anthony Fauci.

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: Tom Selleck says 'Blue Bloods' cast made major sacrifice to save show before cancellation
articles.excerpt:
Donnie Wahlberg and Jenny McCarthy told Fox News Digital that they prefer ordering takeout and watching the faith-based TV show for date nights.

Tom Selleck addressed the "very frustrating" end to "B...
articles.body_text:
Donnie Wahlberg and Jenny McCarthy told Fox News Digital that they prefer ordering takeout and watching the faith-based TV show for date nights.

Tom Selleck addressed the "very frustrating" end to "Blue Bloods," saying the cast had already taken a 25% salary cut to keep it on the air despite it still ranking in sixth place in broadcast shows.

"They claim 14, but it was 15. We did 15 seasons, 293 episodes," Selleck told Ted Danson on his "Where Everybody Knows Your Name" podcast Wednesday. "’Blue Bloods’ was a labor of love for everybody.

"Maybe people don't realize, but a lot of shows become miserable to work on. You get a lot of egos, and ‘I'm not coming out of my dressing room ‘til he's coming out,’ and it's miserable. It's absolutely miserable."

TED DANSON WAS SHOCKED WOMEN VIEWED HIM AS A SEX SYMBOL DURING EARLY ‘CHEERS’ DAYS

Tom Selleck poses with "Blue Bloods" castmates Bridget Moynahan and Donnie Wahlberg in 2014. (GC Images)

But he said "Blue Bloods" was never like that.

Knowing that his character was the patriarch of the family on the show, he decided to "set an example."

"Either way, everybody got it," he continued, saying that, in the last year of the show, "at our last family dinner, everybody wanted to come back. We'd already taken a 25% cut in salary. We'd already done all sorts of things to keep the show going. But the show was, it was very frustrating 'cause ‘Blue Bloods’ was out of the top 100 shows on broadcast television, ‘Blue Bloods’ was No. 6 in our 15th year."

ROSEANNE BARR HASN’T SPOKEN TO TV SISTER LAURIE METCALF SINCE SHOW’S CANCELLATION

The 81-year-old actor reiterated that "nobody wanted to leave. Everybody was gonna stay on. That's hard to get. It may be some kind of record to have the same cast intact for that length of time."

The cast might have made different decisions if it wasn’t a family, "but, you know, you couldn't very well replace Jamie [Will Estes] or Danny [Donnie Wahlberg] or anybody with another actor."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Tom Selleck filming "Blue Bloods" in 2011. (WireImage)

Two years ago, after shooting the final episode, Selleck told TV Insider he was "frustrated" about the show ending because it was still "wildly successful."

"I’m not going to turn into a bitter old guy saying, ‘Get off my lawn!’ I don’t believe in holding grudges, but if you were to say to the television network, ‘Here’s a show you can program in the worst time slot you got, and it is going to guarantee you winning Friday night for the next 15 years,’ it would be almost impossible to believe," he said at the time.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

He added that he felt "Blue Bloods" was "taken for granted because it performed from the get-go. So, how do I feel? It’s going to take a long time to sort all of this out. I remember after the weekend [of the final episode’s shoot], I said, ‘I’ve got to get to bed early tonight because I have to do my dialogue for Monday.’ Well, there was no Monday. It’s just going to take a while."

Donnie Wahlberg shooting "Blue Bloods" in 2016. (CBS via Getty Images)

Last year, Selleck doubted he would reprise his role on Wahlberg’s spin-off, "Boston Blue."

"I don’t know if I would do ‘Boston Blue.’ That’s another show," he told Hour Detroit in November. "I think it’s partly my lot in life to make sure ‘Blue Bloods’ has its place in television history, but I don’t think it’s my lot in life to keep playing Frank Reagan."

Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Europe’s heating climate sparks ‘major intensification’ of fires: Report
articles.excerpt:
Southern Europe is “becoming more flammable,” with the number of summer days featuring conditions likely to produce fires having more than doubled since 1981, according to a new report.

The study, pu...
articles.body_text:
Southern Europe is “becoming more flammable,” with the number of summer days featuring conditions likely to produce fires having more than doubled since 1981, according to a new report.

The study, published on Thursday in the Scientific Reports journal, said that this “major intensification” of fire-prone weather is driven by climate change. It noted that these effects are especially pronounced in France and Spain, which have been battling some of their largest blazes since records began in recent weeks.

The steep increase in the frequency of fire weather – characterised by searing temperatures, low humidity, dryness, and strong winds – “can only be attributed to global warming,” said study co-author Raul Cordero.

European countries are enduring an above-average season for wildfires, and have already overtaken 2025, which was a record-breaking year for destructive blazes.

Cooling weather and rain helped to calm the worst of the fires in France and Spain on Thursday.

France told 84,000 evacuees in the southwest of the country that it was now safe to go home, as France’s largest wildfire since 1949 pulled back.

Spain ended its state of national emergency as wildfires threatening areas near Madrid – the largest Spain has experienced since records began in 1961 – began to come under control.

However, as high temperatures moved eastwards, fires were being fought in Greece, Turkiye, and the United Kingdom.

In Greece, two firefighters died on the island of Crete on Wednesday, the fire department said, as several fires started around the country, fanned by gale-force winds. Another died in a separate fire in the Peloponnese region as the blazes continued into Thursday.

“We have difficult days ahead of us,” Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said.

Firefighters in Turkiye have been battling at least 115 fires across the country, although at least 110 were under control, according to the country’s agriculture minister.

An enormous wildfire has forced evacuations and prompted road closures in eastern England. The fire at Dunwich Heath, a significant biodiversity site, is one of the largest the region has seen.

articles.title: Florida AG threatens Fauci investigation after Senate hearing
articles.excerpt: Dr. Anthony Fauci pleaded the Fifth Amendment over 100 times in a Senate hearing, leading Senator Rand Paul to accuse him of lying and destroying public records related to the COVID-19 pandemic. Paul ...
articles.body_text:
Dr. Anthony Fauci pleaded the Fifth Amendment over 100 times in a Senate hearing, leading Senator Rand Paul to accuse him of lying and destroying public records related to the COVID-19 pandemic. Paul advocates for holding Fauci in contempt of Congress.

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier said he will be opening up an investigation into former National Institutes of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Dr. Anthony Fauci following Fauci's explosive decision to invoke his Fifth Amendment right and not answer any questions during a congressional hearing Wednesday.

"Fauci's lack of candor to Congress is unbelievable. My office is launching an investigation into Dr. Fauci. It's past time we get the truth of what happened during COVID," Uthmeier wrote in a Wednesday post on X.

Uthmeier further expanded on his decision in an exclusive statement to Fox News Digital.

FAUCI PLEADS FIFTH WITH 'ZERO LEGAL JUSTIFICATION' AS CRITICS ERUPT AND DEMAND CONTEMPT CHARGES

James Uthmeier spoke at the National Conservative Convention on Sept. 3, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Dominic Gwinn/Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images)

"In light of recent reports exposed by Senator Rand Paul, we will investigate any and all potential violations of Florida law involving Anthony Fauci," Uthmeier told Fox News Digital.

"Our inquiry will focus on what Fauci knew, when he knew it, and how he misled the American people. We will examine the physical and monetary harms to Floridians that may have resulted from his deceptions and determine whether his conduct exposes him to liability under state law," Uthmeier's statement concluded.

Uthmeier cited revelations published by Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee Chairman Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., which revealed internal notes Fauci wrote on government computers during his time at NIAID.

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

Former NIH Director Anthony Fauci listens during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee hearing on July 29, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Fauci declined to answer questions, asserting his Fifth Amendment right. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

The internal notes, which Paul and others have taken to referring to as Fauci's "diary," suggest Fauci appeared to publicly overstate the death rate from COVID-19 compared to what he wrote privately.

"[Former CDC Director] Tom Frieden called me this AM and we discussed various aspects of the outbreak," Fauci wrote on Feb. 8, 2020.

"He and I are on the same page in thinking tht [sic] this is acting like a bad influenza in its transmissibility and that the denominator is much greater than 34,867 (above) making the case fatality rate (CFR) more like 0.2-0.3 % rather than 2.0%," Fauci's entry concluded.

However, a month later, in congressional testimony to the House Oversight Committee on March 11, 2020, Fauci pegged the mortality rate at 1%.

"I think if you count all the cases of minimally symptomatic or asymptomatic infection, that probably brings the mortality rate down to somewhere around one percent, which means it is 10 times more lethal than the seasonal flu," he testified.

Anthony Fauci declined to testify in a Senate committee hearing on his role in the US response to COVID-19, invoking his Fifth Amendment rights. (Left (Alex WROBLEWSKI / AFP via Getty Images), Right (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images))

When called to testify on the revelations before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Wednesday, Fauci exercised his Fifth Amendment right and refused to answer legislators' questions 111 times.

Uthmeier is not the only Republican to take aim at the former COVID czar Fauci in light of the revelations.

Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, said Wednesday that Fauci should be held in congressional contempt for refusing to answer questions despite receiving a presidential pardon.

"I think Anthony Fauci has had contempt for Congress and contempt for the American people for decades," he said. "His diary shows that he deliberately lied to the American people over and over and over again," Cruz said.

Paul, for his part, said his committee will vote on whether to hold Fauci in contempt next week.

articles.title: Online fury erupts as conservatives recall ’insane’ COVID-19 lockdown policies after Fauci takes the Fifth
articles.excerpt: Senator Ted Cruz alleges Dr. Anthony Fauci repeatedly lied to Congress and the public, evidenced by private diaries from the COVID-19 pandemic. Cruz claims Fauci knew the virus did not originate in a ...
articles.body_text:
Senator Ted Cruz alleges Dr. Anthony Fauci repeatedly lied to Congress and the public, evidenced by private diaries from the COVID-19 pandemic. Cruz claims Fauci knew the virus did not originate in a wet market and was covering his involvement in gain-of-function research.

Conservatives aren't willing to forgive and forget the COVID-19 lockdowns — a fact made clear online as fury erupted during and after Dr. Anthony Fauci's appearance before Congress on Wednesday where he repeatedly invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination.

Those who opposed the lockdowns, which Fauci bragged about helping implement in his now-infamous diary but extensively denied implementing publicly, had a field day online recalling the policies pushed by the one-time White House health advisor.

"Reminder how how insane the world was in 2021," Dr. Mollie James, a trauma surgeon and internet personality, said on X. She was commenting on a video of professional golfer Jon Rahm, who was forced to withdraw from a PGA Tour event while holding a six stroke lead because he tested positive for the virus while he was on the golf course.

The winner of that tournament earned north of $1.6 million.

New York, NY, USA - April 6, 2020: A man wearing protective mask crosses 6th Avenue of Americas in Midtown Manhattan deserted because of the city lockdown caused by COVID-19 pandemic. (iStock)

FAUCI PRIVATELY TOOK CREDIT FOR COVID-19 LOCKDOWNS DESPITE PUBLIC DENIAL, NEWLY EXPOSED DIARY ENTRIES REVEAL

"Never forget that California arrested a man for paddleboarding alone to keep him safe from COVID," recalled conservative activist Alex Lorusso, who goes by @alx on X. "Most retarded time period in human history."

The Malibu paddleboarder, who was alone on the water, was arrested on a misdemeanor charge of disobeying a lifeguard after allegedly violating Los Angeles' lockdown orders.

"Dr. Fauci isn't the only guilty one," Rep. Lance Gooden, D-Texas, said on X. "Democrats went as far as filling outdoor skate parks with sand to enforce their draconian COVID-19 lockdowns. Americans should never forget what they did."

Along with the post, he added a viral video showing a backhoe shoveling sand into a Venice Beach skate park.

Former NIH Director Anthony Fauci listens during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee hearing on July 29, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Fauci declined to answer questions, asserting his Fifth Amendment right. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

LEGACY MEDIA COVERS ANTHONY FAUCI DIARY BY CRITICIZING DONALD TRUMP INSTEAD OF FAUCI'S DISHONESTY

Kelly McCarty, a very outspoken critic of lockdowns and mRNA vaccines, posted a video of Ohio mother Alecia Ketts being tased and arrested by a school resource officer after refusing to wear a mask while watching a football game outside.

Ketts was with her children at the time. She later pleaded no contest to a trespassing charge.

Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, referenced Ketts during his Wednesday grilling of Fauci, who was ordered to appear before the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Moreno attributed his run for Senate to COVID-era government restrictions.

A person passes a storefront with a sign posted that masks are required on Oak Street in Copiague, New York on May 18, 2022. (Steve Pfost/Newsday RM via Getty Images)

TOP 5 MOMENTS FROM FAUCI'S HEARING: PAUL BOOTS LAWYER, MORENO ERUPTS AS CONTEMPT VOTE LOOMS

During the Senate hearing, Fauci pleaded the Fifth 111 times. He refused to answer a single question posed by the senators, including what day of the week it was and what color tie he was wearing.

Podcast host Alex Lace noted to his nearly 58,000 X followers the time when high school track runners were forced to wear masks during meets.

"I s--- you not. During COVID they forced high school track teams to run outdoors… in masks," he said, later adding, "Never forget what they did."

Demonstrators take part in Operation Grid-Lock to Re-Open New York to protest against lockdown measures in the wake, during the outbreak of the coronavirus disease (COVID-19), at the New York State Capitol in Albany, New York, U.S., April 22, 2020. REUTERS/Bryan R Smith (REUTERS/Bryan R Smith)

Popular X user Chaya Raichik, who runs the LibsOfTikTok account also posted an image of news headlines detailing politicians and public figures who broke their own lockdown rules.

Examples include Democrat Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer apparently bucking her own rules to party at a dive bar; Democrat California Gov. Gavin Newsom attending a party at swanky Napa Valley restaurant French Laundry while his own lockdown orders lingered; and Washington, D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser officiating an indoor wedding without a mask mere hours after issuing an indoor mask order.

"It’s insane that any of these people were ever taken seriously again after this," post was captioned.

Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Trump says he may ‘temporarily’ drop bid to make Blanche US attorney general
articles.excerpt:
President says he has no objection to pulling his former lawyer’s name until dissenting Republicans are out of office

Donald Trump said on Thursday he may “temporarily” pull the nomination of Todd Bl...
articles.body_text:
President says he has no objection to pulling his former lawyer’s name until dissenting Republicans are out of office

Donald Trump said on Thursday he may “temporarily” pull the nomination of Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general, but would keep him in the role in an acting capacity until two Republican senators objecting to his confirmation leave office next year – an extraordinary escalation of an intra-party fight over an agreement to create a $1.8bn slush fund and give the president tax immunity.

Two Republican senators – John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina – have refused to back Blanche’s nomination until they receive written confirmation from the justice department that it is not moving forward with a widely criticized agreement creating a $1.8bn fund to compensate people claiming they were targets of political weaponization and granting the president, his family and business entities broad immunity from past tax investigations.

Blanche has already said publicly that the payout fund to compensate victims of so-called government weaponization is not moving forward amid bipartisan backlash. But Cornyn and Tillis had sought assurances in writing, something Blanche has refused to do. Cornyn also sought to clarify the terms of the tax immunity portion of the agreement.

The Senate judiciary committee cancelled a vote on Blanche’s confirmation scheduled for Thursday when it became clear he did not have the votes to advance. The two senators – who are both leaving Congress in January – appeared to be negotiating language with the justice department on Wednesday.

On Thursday, Trump blasted Cornyn and Tillis and vowed that he would instead keep Blanche, Trump’s former personal lawyer, as the acting attorney general – a role he has held since April when Pam Bondi resigned. Federal law allows the deputy attorney general – Blanche’s role under Bondi – to serve indefinitely as the acting attorney general until a successor is confirmed.

“John Cornyn, of Texas, and Thom Tillis, of North Carolina, both of whom I refused to Endorse, and whose political careers have been ended by my action, are refusing to vote for this Great Nominee, who will remain, in any event, as Acting.

“I have no objection to temporarily withdrawing Todd’s name, if they do not do the right thing, and putting him back after Cornyn and Tillis are out of office,” Trump posted.

Cornyn, who lost his re-election bid to a Trump-endorsed rival, responded by saying “POTUS is mistaken if he believes concerns about the provisions in his tax lawsuit settlement are limited to me and Senator Tillis.”

Tillis, who is not seeking re-election after repeated clashes with Trump, told reporters on Capitol Hill: “It makes no sense to me. This is not popular.”

“The president’s not winning on this issue,” he continued. “It is killing some of our candidates because they can’t explain it. And now it looks like they weren’t being honest when they said it was inoperative.”

Earlier on Thursday, both Cornyn and Tillis had expressed a willingness to vote for Blanche.

“If this were just between me and Todd Blanche, we would have worked this out, but, apparently, he’s getting some pushback from higher ups at the White House. I don’t know who, but it doesn’t need to be this hard,” Cornyn said on Capitol Hill.

The agreement was reached as part of a settlement in a lawsuit Trump filed against the IRS over the unauthorized leak of his tax returns. A federal judge who oversaw the lawsuit blasted the arrangement, noting that the justice department did not make a good faith effort to defend the government and that it appeared to be a collusive effort to engineer a beneficial result on behalf of the president.

Blanche needs the vote of every Republican on the Senate judiciary committee, including Cornyn and Tillis, to advance his nomination to land the role on a permanent basis.

articles.title: Kamala Harris' new $8M mansion is in a neighborhood with virtually no Black residents
articles.excerpt: Fox News contributor Marc Thiessen, a former speechwriter for George W. Bush, discusses big donors' skepticism toward Kamala Harris' 2028 presidential run. Thiessen points to her past campaign's strug...
articles.body_text:
Fox News contributor Marc Thiessen, a former speechwriter for George W. Bush, discusses big donors' skepticism toward Kamala Harris' 2028 presidential run. Thiessen points to her past campaign's struggles and perceived left-wing stance as reasons for donor reluctance, highlighting her position to the left of Bernie Sanders in voting record analysis.

Despite a career-long commitment to combatting racial disparities in housing and touting the importance of living among Black people, former Vice President Kamala Harris’s new California mansion is situated in a neighborhood with virtually no racial diversity.

Harris’s new 4,000-square-foot property, which reports indicate she acquired for $8.15 million, is located in the exclusive seaside community of Point Dume and includes ocean views, multiple wine fridges, private golf greens and enough parking to accommodate five vehicles.

Point Dume is situated entirely within Census tract 8004.08, which the Census Bureau’s American Community Survey estimated was just 0.2% Black and roughly 94% White as of 2019.

Harris's choice of neighborhood may surprise longtime observers given past comments she has made about the importance of living among other Black Americans.

KAMALA HARRIS IS THE 'FAIRLY OBVIOUS' 2028 PRESIDENTIAL FRONTRUNNER, DEMOCRATIC INSIDERS SAY

Despite a career-long commitment to combatting racial disparities in housing and touting the importance of living among Black people, former Vice President Kamala Harris’s new California mansion is situated in a neighborhood with virtually no racial diversity. (Johnny Nunez/WireImage; Kevin Carter/Getty Images)

"When you’re at (a historically black college or university), and especially one with the size and with the history of Howard University — and also in the context of also being in D.C., which was known forever as being ‘Chocolate City’ — it just becomes about you understanding that there is a whole world of people who are like you," Harris told a Washington Post reporter in 2019, reflecting on her experience growing up in primarily White social circles then attending a historically Black college in a predominantly African American city.

"It was more, for me, about the numerosity than it was the diversity, I grew up in a community where there were many representations of diversity," she added. "Going to Howard, there were so many (Black people)! And they’re all in your age group, in your phase of life."

Now, however, Harris has chosen to put roots down in a community that at least one group has accused of trying to keep their beaches closed off to minorities.

CHICAGO SUBURB LOCALS HOPE REPARATIONS ADDRESSES 'AFFORDABILITY PRESSURES' AS BLACK POPULATION DWINDLES

Vice President Kamala Harris, California Gov. Gavin Newsom and California First Partner Jennifer Siebel Newsom wave during a campaign rally opposing the gubernatorial recall election on Sept. 8, 2021, in San Leandro, California.  (Kent Nishimura / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

"Despite the veneer of a laid back community of surfers who are one with nature, there are barriers to access that keep most BIPOC people away," a pair of non-White surfers wrote in a 2025 review of Harris’s new neighborhood.

Harris spent a sizable portion of her career working to tear down similar barriers.

HARRIS STOPS IN KEY PRESIDENTIAL PRIMARY STATE AFTER LEAVING DOOR WIDE OPEN TO 2028 RUN

Vice President Kamala Harris hugs Second Gentleman Douglas Emhoff after speaking on the final day of the Democratic National Convention at the United Center in Chicago, Ill., on Aug. 22, 2024. (Andrew Caballero-Reynolds/AFP)

In 2012, as California’s attorney general, for instance, she joined a Supreme Court brief arguing that the Fair Housing Act can be enforced when policies have a "disparate impact" across different racial groups, even if the policies themselves are racially neutral.

As a presidential candidate, she proposed $100 billion in assistance for families in historically redlined communities and as vice president she promoted the Biden administration’s efforts to combat racial bias in home appraisals.

During Harris’s 2020 presidential campaign, she faced questions about the authenticity of her African American identity due to her Indian and Jamaican heritage and upbringing in affluent, primarily White areas. The attacks resurfaced in 2024, when then-candidate Donald Trump accused Harris of using her Black identity for political gain.

Harris caught flak during the 2024 campaign for identifying with Oakland, California, even though she spent most of her childhood growing up in Berkeley, California, which was significantly less racially diverse. As a teenager, she moved to Montreal, another predominantly White city, with her mother.

Doug Emhoff, Harris' husband, is also White.

Harris has returned to the headlines in recent weeks amid speculation that she may make a third run for the presidency in 2028.

A representative for the former vice president did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital Wednesday.

articles.title: Capital culture war heats up as GOP lawmaker targets DC schools over Old Glory snub
articles.excerpt:
Education Secretary Linda McMahon discusses the lack of patriotism and civic education in schools on ‘America 250: Celebrating Freedom.’

FIRST ON FOX: Florida Republican Sen. Ashley Moody introduced ...
articles.body_text:
Education Secretary Linda McMahon discusses the lack of patriotism and civic education in schools on ‘America 250: Celebrating Freedom.’

FIRST ON FOX: Florida Republican Sen. Ashley Moody introduced a bill targeting the Washington, D.C. public school system in a push to prioritize patriotism in the nation’s capital, Fox News Digital has learned.

The PLEDGE Act proposal would require teachers to feature the American Flag in their classrooms, and for administrators to provide students the opportunity to recite the Pledge of Allegiance every day.

"Currently, there are schools in Washington, D.C., the nation’s capital, that do not display our flag or set aside time for students to recite the Pledge of Allegiance, but they do teach them to be activists," claims the press release shared with Fox News Digital.

FAR-LEFT ACTIVIST CONFERENCE AT TEACHERS UNION HQ RAISES CLASSROOM CONCERNS

Activists burns a U.S. flag at Black Lives Matter Plaza near the White House July 4, 2020 in Washington, DC. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

In a city where Pride flags and progressive causes are prominently displayed across the district, some conservatives say patriotic symbols like the American Flag have taken a back seat in schools — fueling concerns about how civic values are being taught to the next generations of Americans.

"Radicals want to teach kids to be ashamed of the United States of America and how to be activists instead. We should be teaching kids why America is worth loving, and most importantly, the principles and values that make America worth defending," said Sen. Moody in the release.

Over 40 states have varying Pledge requirements in their schools — but not in the nation’s capital.

"My PLEDGE Act helps restore pride in our nation by reminding students every day of the freedom, responsibilities, and blessings that come with being an American, and the sacrifices made for our flag and everything it represents," Moody said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital.

BERNIE SANDERS, DSA REVEAL DEMANDS FOR DEM PARTY AFTER SOCIALISTS SWEEP NEW YORK ELECTIONS

Protestors repaint "Defund the Police" on Black Lives Matter Plaza on the final night of the Republican National Convention, August 27, 2020. (Evelyn Hockstein/For The Washington Post via Getty Images)

The bill comes amid a mayoral race in D.C., where socialist candidate Janeese Lewis George is the frontrunner. This continues a trend in the nationwide rise of the far-left Democratic Socialist of America (DSA) movement, which often spouts anti-American rhetoric.

The DSA platform, which aims to appeal to younger voters, wants to replace free-market capitalism with social ownership. It also pushes for major constitutional changes, like abolishing the Electoral College and expanding voting rights for noncitizens.

Younger Americans are significantly less likely to express strong national pride than older generations, with just 41% of Generation Z saying they are extremely or very proud to be American, according to a June 2025 Gallup poll.

The same poll says 58% of U.S. adults say they are "extremely" or "very" proud to be American, the lowest level the pollsters have recorded since it began asking the question in 2001.

DEMS PUT ON BLAST OVER POLL THAT SHOWS RECORD-LOW PATRIOTISM IN US: 'TEAR OUR SOCIETY APART'

The DC Public School (DCPS) curriculum calls for students to learn more progressive politics, from studying Harvey Milk to learning how the LGBTQ+ community has shaped and defined the Washington, D.C. community.

For example, 5th grade social studies standards in the district require students to analyze the rise of queer culture during the Black Renaissance and also require students to compare the experiences of LGBTQ+ service members returning to the U.S. after World War II, according to their 2023 Social Study Standards.

UNITED STATES - OCTOBER 21: Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., leaves the Senate floor after a vote in the U.S. Capitol on Tuesday, October 21, 2025. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

During President Donald Trump's second term, his administration restored patriotic symbols to the nation's capital by installing two large American flags on the White House grounds and removing the "Black Lives Matter" street mural on the plaza just blocks from the executive residence.

Washington, D.C., has long been a focal point for political demonstrations and protests. Trump, in his second term, deployed the National Guard to help bolster safety in the city.

Fox News Digital reached out to DCPS for comment.

READ THE FULL TEXT OF THE PROPOSED LEGISLATION:

Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.
