articles.title: Minnesota Vikings suspend defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander after DWI guilty plea
articles.excerpt: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith is cited for speeding and not having his driver's license in Davie, Florida, marking his third encounter with the Davie Police Department this offseason (Credit: D...
articles.body_text:
New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith is cited for speeding and not having his driver's license in Davie, Florida, marking his third encounter with the Davie Police Department this offseason (Credit: Davie Police Department).

Another NFL assistant coach is being disciplined by his team after facing driving under the influence allegations, this time with Minnesota Vikings defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander being suspended by the team.

The Vikings announced Tuesday that Alexander has been suspended for three weeks after he pleaded guilty to driving while intoxicated earlier this month. Alexander's blood alcohol level was 0.169, or more than twice Minnesota's legal limit, on an initial breathalyzer test, according to the charging statement.

Alexander, hired in February as the team's passing game coordinator as well as defensive backs coach, was arrested in April, and his guilty plea came on July 16.

NFL SUSPENDS ARIZONA CARDINALS EXECUTIVE FOR VIOLATING GAMBLING POLICY, LEAKING DRAFT INFO

Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell reacts during the second half at Soldier Field on Sept. 8, 2025. (Matt Marton/Imagn Images)

Alexander pleaded guilty to third-degree DWI, a misdemeanor, and paid $603 in fines and fees. He was assigned 48 hours of community service and will be on probation for two years.

Alexander's club suspension began on July 24, although it was not announced then. It will run through Aug. 13.

"Following Gerald’s arrest earlier this spring, we remained in communication with the NFL while awaiting the outcome of the legal process," the Vikings said in a statement. "We take these situations seriously and believe this disciplinary action is appropriate."

The NFL tells Fox News Digital the club suspension will close the matter and Alexander will not be subject to additional league discipline under the personal conduct policy.

Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores looks on during the fourth quarter of a game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on Jan. 4, 2026. (Matt Blewett/Imagn Images)

Alexander, who previously worked under Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores in Miami when Flores was the head coach, also released a statement through the team.

"I take full responsibility for the situation I put myself in and apologize for not meeting the mark," Alexander said. "I know it’s unacceptable. I understand the suspension and am committed to learning from the matter and ensuring I come back a better version of myself."

TONY ROMO ARRESTED IN MILWAUKEE FOR ALLEGED OWI OFFENSE: REPORT

Alexander is the second NFL assistant coach to face team discipline for offseason troubles with DWI.

The Washington Commanders on Monday announced the firing of assistant coach Ben Steele just days before the start of training camp.

Arizona Cardinals tight ends coach Ben Steele oversees practice during the NFL game between the Arizona Cardinals and Houston Texans on Nov. 19, 2023, at NRG Stadium in Houston, Texas. (Icon Sportswire)

Steele, who was serving as the team's tight ends coach, was hired by the Commanders this offseason.

"We are parting ways with tight ends coach Ben Steele. The team will have no further comment at this time," the Commanders said in a statement.

The Athletic reported that Steele was arrested on suspicion of DWI in June. He is facing an additional charge for refusing a blood/breath test and obstructing or resisting an officer without force, per the report.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Steele had previously been under suspension by the Commanders.

These two issues coming to light in the same week suggest some coaches may need more extensive training or onboarding to make clear the pitfalls of drinking — even away from the club.

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: Haley Stevens shreds Abdul El-Sayed: 'We don't need a celebrity candidate'
articles.excerpt: Rep. Haley Stevens accused Michigan Democratic Senate rival Abdul El-Sayed of chasing celebrity during the FOX 2 Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate primary debate at the network’s studios in Southfield, ...
articles.body_text:
Rep. Haley Stevens accused Michigan Democratic Senate rival Abdul El-Sayed of chasing celebrity during the FOX 2 Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate primary debate at the network’s studios in Southfield, Michigan, on July 27, 2026. (Credit: WJBK)

Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., repeatedly called Abdul El-Sayed the "celebrity" candidate in the Michigan Senate race during Monday's Senate Democratic debate, arguing that El-Sayed's podcast, books and political activism pale in comparison to her time in Congress.

The race between Stevens and El-Sayed has become a microcosm of the battle over the Democratic Party's future. On Aug. 4, Democratic voters will decide whether to back Stevens, who has the support of the Democratic establishment, or El-Sayed, a socialist-supported challenger who has called for abolishing ICE and is strongly critical of the United States' support for Israel.

In her opening remarks, Stevens rattled off her qualifications as the Democratic Party's best chance of winning the Senate race, pointing to flipping her seat in 2018, being named Michigan's most effective Democratic lawmaker by the Center for Effective Lawmaking in 2025 and being endorsed by Democratic Michigan Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer.

"My only focus is you," Stevens said. "Abdul is running for celebrity. Republicans are propping up his campaign, and Mike Rogers, just the other day said in a secret phone call that he made it easier for him to win, that he's the one he wants to run against."

DEM CIVIL WAR HITS PRIMARY DEBATE STAGE IN FIERY BATTLEGROUND SHOWDOWN: 'WHAT ARE YOU HIDING?'

Retiring Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich., has abandoned his neutrality in Michigan's high-stakes Democratic Senate primary, backing U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens, pictured left, as party leaders rally to stop progressive rival Abdul El-Sayed, pictured right, from winning the nomination. (AP Photo/Kristen Norman)

Stevens was referring to a phone conversation Republican candidate Mike Rogers had with supporters last month in which he said his campaign would be in "good shape" if El-Sayed were the nominee.

"Look, this isn't about the D.C. or New York influencer crowd," Stevens said. "This is about putting Michigan first."

Later in the debate, Stevens said she is standing up to Trump's "abuses of powers," while taking a dig at Abdul by saying she's doing so without "shouting into a bullhorn, not getting in front of the first camera I see, but doing the hard work."

SWING-STATE POLL SPELLS TROUBLE FOR FAR LEFT AS SCHUMER-BACKED CANDIDATE DOMINATES WITH CRITICAL VOTING BLOCS

Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., speaks during a rally on the West Front of the U.S. Capitol to support research and policies for breast cancer treatment that are at risk by proposed Medicaid cuts, on Tuesday, May 6, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

"Look, my opponent here, Abdul, he is such a talented guy," Stevens said, referring to his three books and his podcast America Dissected. "He's had all this attention, but the deal is, we don't need a celebrity candidate. We don't need a celebrity."

Stevens then pointed to her six years in the House of Representatives, saying she has been committed to "hard, unglamorous work."

"That's going to stand up to this junk that is wreaking havoc and causing chaos right before our very eyes," Stevens said.

Stevens suggested that Abdul's Senate campaign is just another "rung on the ladder" for him, pointing to his failed 2018 gubernatorial bid.

"It didn't work out, so he started the podcast, he wrote the books, and now he's running for Senate, and he's already bought the website for president," Stevens said.

In response, El-Sayed accused Stevens of "cowardice" over her past votes to increase ICE funding, saying the agency should be completely abolished.

MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ABDUL EL-SAYED DODGES QUESTION ON WHETHER HE STILL SUPPORTS DEFUNDING THE POLICE

"So yeah, I’m going to take the bullhorn and I’m going to say that I think we need to abolish ICE because I am not afraid of what they’re going to say about me," he said.

He also suggested that Stevens' focus on his public health podcast was a distraction from the issues that matter most to voters, such as affordability.

"Congresswoman, if you enjoy podcasts about public health, I welcome you to take a listen. You seem very concerned about that," El-Sayed said. "I’m more concerned about the fact that people can’t pay for their gas, they can’t pay for their groceries."

The open Senate race in Michigan has garnered national attention, with outside groups spending more than $52 million on the race through mid-July, most of it in support of Stevens, according to an OpenSecrets analysis of FEC reports.

U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate primary candidate Abdul El-Sayed and U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt, greet the crowd after El-Sayed spoke at The People V. The Powerful rally at the Detroit Opera House on July 18, 2026, in Detroit, Mich. (Sarah Rice/Getty Images)

El-Sayed, who is backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, D-Vt., has painted Stevens as the candidate of large super PACs such as AIPAC, while saying he has not received a single dollar from corporate interests or super PACs. Before running for Congress, El-Sayed served as Wayne County director of Health and Human Services.

Meanwhile, the Republican Party has deemed Michigan to be one of best pickup opportunities in its effort to maintain control of the Senate.

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed and Stevens' campaigns for comment.

Elaine Mallon is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business covering national politics.

articles.title: Marcus Mumford says Bible camp sparked decades-long love story with wife Carey Mulligan

Before Marcus Mumford and Carey Mulligan became one of Hollywood's most private couples, they were just two kids who met at Bible ca...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Before Marcus Mumford and Carey Mulligan became one of Hollywood's most private couples, they were just two kids who met at Bible camp.

The Mumford & Sons frontman recalled on the "SmartLess" podcast how a chance childhood meeting eventually blossomed into romance years later after the pair reconnected as adults.

The future couple first crossed paths at a church Bible camp, when Mumford was 10 and Mulligan was 12, and became pen pals.

JESSIE JAMES DECKER ON WHY HER MARRIAGE TO ERIC DECKER HASN'T LOST ITS SPARK AFTER FOUR KIDS

Marcus Mumford revealed that he first met future wife Carey Mulligan at a church Bible camp when he was 10 and she was 12, years before the pair reconnected and fell in love as adults. (Jenny Anderson/Disney via Getty Images)

"And she still has the journal entry from the day we met where I – my cousin was there, who was two years older, who was age appropriate for her," Mumford recalled. "And he got an eight-and-a-half out of 10. But I, who was definitely not underlined boyfriend material, got a nine out 10."

The flattering review didn't spark an instant romance, but it planted the seed for a relationship that would take years to come together.

He recalled the two "stayed in touch as kids" before reconnecting in their twenties on Facebook. Mulligan bought a ticket to Laura Marling's show years later, where Mumford & Sons was also performing.

Marcus Mumford reflected on his longtime romance with Carey Mulligan, recalling how a childhood friendship that began at Bible camp eventually led to their 2012 wedding. (Dave Benett/Getty Images for Spotify)

LAINEY WILSON ADMITS SHE LIED TO FIANCÉ DUCK HODGES ON THEIR FIRST DATE

"We started shouting sort of an hour before Laura went on and then [Mulligan] was like, 'Oh, Mumford. I knew a kid called Mumford,'" the singer-songwriter recalled.

Mulligan left a note with Mumford's tour manager that had her email address on it and the rest is history.

After dating for roughly five months, Mumford proposed to Mulligan. The two married in front of friends and family in Somerset, England, on April 21, 2012. Mumford and Mulligan share three children together, two daughters and a son.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Carey Mulligan and Marcus Mumford have kept their 14-year marriage largely out of the spotlight after reconnecting as adults following a childhood friendship that began at Bible camp. (Christopher Polk/Getty Images)

The couple is notoriously private about their 14-year marriage.

"Marcus is the only thing that’s mine that I can keep totally away, so I try to," Mulligan told Vogue in 2015.

Throughout the years, Mumford and Mulligan have focused on making their marriage "the priority" in their lives.

"We said, ‘The odds are stacked against us. Let’s make that our great work and everything else can come from that, right?’" Mumford told GQ in 2022. "The reason I think people don’t stay married is because they don’t realize how much work it takes."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Marcus Mumford shared new details about his love story with Carey Mulligan, revealing the Oscar-nominated actress kept a journal entry from the day the pair first met as children. (Gotham/Getty Images)

Mulligan is a British actress known for her roles in "An Education," "Drive," "The Great Gatsby," "Promising Young Woman" and "Maestro," the latter earning her a third Oscar nomination.

Mumford, raised in England, is best known as the lead singer, guitarist and songwriter for Mumford & Sons, the Grammy-winning folk-rock band that helped define the early 2010s folk revival.

articles.title: Wisconsin brewery that offered 'free beer' when Trump dies says alcohol permit revoked
articles.excerpt: ‘The Big Weekend Show’ co-hosts discuss a Wisconsin brewery facing renewed scrutiny after the White House Correspondents’ Dinner shooting and influencer Hasan Piker’s comments in a New York Times inte...
articles.body_text:
‘The Big Weekend Show’ co-hosts discuss a Wisconsin brewery facing renewed scrutiny after the White House Correspondents’ Dinner shooting and influencer Hasan Piker’s comments in a New York Times interview.

A Wisconsin brewery known for anti-Trump social media posts, including one promising a free beer promotion upon the death of President Donald Trump, has had its permit to operate in the state revoked by state officials.

The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported Monday that liberal activist and brewery owner Kirk Bangstad is "vowing to fight ‘tooth and nail’ after receiving a letter from the state's Department of Revenue revoking Minocqua Brewing Co.'s permit to operate in Wisconsin, according to a July 26 newsletter sent to his supporters."

"As you can imagine, I’m not taking this lying down," Bangstad wrote in a Substack post on Sunday. "We’re going to fight the state of Wisconsin tooth and nail, and once again, they’ll have to pry me out of my taprooms before I stop selling beer to thirsty progressives who come to visit us."

WISCONSIN DEM'S BAR LAMENTS 'WE ALMOST GOT FREE BEER DAY' FOR TRUMP ASSASSINATION

President Donald Trump took a victory lap over a judge's ruling allowing his legal team to amend his $15 billion defamation lawsuit against The New York Times. (Eric Lee/Getty Images)

He also asked readers to donate to his legal defense fund, writing, "As usual, fighting to keep my business alive means I have to pay lawyers, and that’s never cheap. Every time this [happens], I rack up $100K in legal bills before we even see a judge. If you can help chip in to the Minocqua Company’s legal defense fund, I’d really appreciate it."

The revocation of the beer license goes into effect on Aug. 4, the Sentinel reported. The business has locations in Madison and Minocqua.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the Wisconsin Department of Revenue said, "The Wisconsin Division of Alcohol Beverages is dedicated to the fair and consistent enforcement of alcohol beverages regulations in Wisconsin. The division is required to follow and implement state law, including ensuring permit holders and licensees follow all applicable laws and regulations. The division takes appropriate actions when these laws are not followed."

The spokesperson added, "We can confirm that the Department of Revenue has issued notice of a Brewer's permit revocation for two Minocqua Brewing Company locations and notice of an Alcohol Beverage Warehouse permit revocation for one location. The business has until August 4th to appeal and can operate during the appeal process. Should the business decide to appeal, the next step would be to appeal to the Secretary of the Department of Revenue, who will assign the appeal to a Department of Revenue hearing examiner for their recommendations as to proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law."

The Sentinel reported that state regulators pursued revoking Bangstad's alcohol license after authorities seized canned beer from his company in June, alleging it had been transported from Illinois without the required permits and taxes. The newspaper also reported that Bangstad criticized the proposed action as an excessive response, arguing the alleged tax violations did not warrant shutting down his business.

'FREE BEER' FOR TRUMP DEATH DEM ACTIVIST RUNNING FOR WISCONSIN GOV: 'I WILL WIN' IF THEY SILENCE ME

The Minocqua Brewing Company is under fire again for explosive calls for political violence against President Donald Trump. (Minocqua Brewing Company/Facebook)

On Jan. 22, the Minocqua Brewing Company appeared to suggest it would give free beer to patrons if Trump was killed, and while not explicitly using his name, posted on Facebook, "Free beer, all day long the day he dies."

The post continued, "Show us this post when it happens in a few months and we’ll make good on that promise."

The post was updated to say, "we meant the Madison Taproom because that’s open all year, if he dies in the summer, then it’s gonna be the Minocqua Taproom."

In reply to comment on the post, the company also did not refer to Trump by name but said that the post hinted at a high-profile figure when asked whether the timeline for the deal could be moved up earlier.

"Well that's up to you and your ability to act like a cia [sic] agent," the company wrote.

WHCA DINNER SHOOTING SUSPECT COLE ALLEN PLEADS NOT GUILTY, JUDGE SCOFFS AT DEFENSE’S POWER PLAY

Kirk Bangstad says he will fight the Wisconsin Department of Revenue's revocation of Minocqua Brewing Company's alcohol permit set to take effect Aug. 4. (Getty Images)

Following the April shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner where Trump was present, the company wrote on Facebook, "Well, we almost got #freebeerday."

"Either a brother or sister in the Resistance needs to work on their marksmanship or he faked another assassination to get a positive news cycle," the post added. "We’ll never know. Regardless, we stand at the ready to pour free beer the day it happens."

Bangstad, the owner of the brewery, is also the founder of the Minocqua Brewing Company SuperPAC, which "aims to remove Republican federal and state elected officials who perpetuated the election lies that caused the Insurrection of January 6, 2021, and whose downplaying of the seriousness of COVID-19 caused so many unnecessary deaths in our country," according to the brewery’s website.

Reached for comment by Fox News Digital, Bangstad declined to comment directly but made jokes about the deaths of Trump and Mitch McConnell and made disparaging remarks about Fox.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The brewery states on its website that it "started making #progressivebeer after closing our brewpub because Donald Trump played politics with Covid-19 and Mitch McConnell let restaurants twist in the wind." (iStock)

Rachel del Guidice is a culture reporter for Fox News covering the intersection of politics, faith, family, and American culture.

articles.title: Trump reportedly pushing RFK Jr to cut vaccines more aggressively
articles.excerpt:
White House has halted changing vaccine schedule as it is unpopular, but anti-vaxx Trump set on ‘alleviating autism’

Donald Trump is pushing the longtime vaccine opponent and current health secretary...
articles.body_text:
White House has halted changing vaccine schedule as it is unpopular, but anti-vaxx Trump set on ‘alleviating autism’

Donald Trump is pushing the longtime vaccine opponent and current health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr to be more aggressive on cutting vaccines in the US, according to reporting from the Wall Street Journal.

Trump has a long record of anti-vaccine statements, but the White House recently put a hold on vaccine changes after polling indicated they were a losing issue in the midterm elections.

Kennedy, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services, recently slashed the routine childhood immunization schedule in an unprecedented move.

Trump reportedly asked Kennedy at his northern Virginia golf course in May if the health secretary had the “yips”, according to the Journal.

Trump wasn’t talking about a sudden inability to make putts. Kennedy wasn’t making enough cuts to the US vaccination schedule, Trump reportedly said.

The US president hopes to make “alleviating autism” a component of his legacy, the Journal reported – and he has taken issue with Kennedy’s less aggressive changes to vaccination recommendations in recent months.

“Donald Trump has been anti-vaccine at least since 2015,” said Paul Offit, director of the Vaccine Education Center and an infectious diseases physician at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia. At the Republican primary debate that year, Trump said that autism had gotten “totally out of control” and vaccines should be in “smaller doses over a longer period of time”.

Trump regularly posted on social media about debunked links between vaccination and autism as early as 2014, and his posts on Truth Social have recently advocated for breaking up shots into individual components and delaying some childhood vaccines for more than a decade.

Tony Fabrizio, a top pollster for Trump, found that anti-vaccine moves are unpopular with voters in key districts, concluding in a December memo that “skepticism toward vaccine requirements is politically risky for both parties”.

Susie Wiles gave HHS the deadline of New Year’s Eve to make vaccine changes, to allow vaccines to fall into the background with the midterms looming, according to reporting by the Rolling Stone.

But Trump’s priorities appear to lie elsewhere. He issued a memo, two days after Fabrizio’s poll results, directing HHS to align with “peer” nations on vaccination recommendations, even though the US was already making similar recommendations to other countries.

A month later, Kennedy slashed vaccine recommendations by one-third, from 17 to 11. A federal judge ordered a halt to these changes following a lawsuit in March from the American Academy of Pediatrics. The judge also paused the work of the advisory committee on immunization practices (ACIP), which was illegally formed under Kennedy, he said.

Kennedy has not made any significant changes to the vaccine schedule since then, though he has continued speaking about autism and its potential causes, and the US government is appealing the judge’s stay on vaccine changes.

Kennedy also sought to divert $5bn in funding – more than 10% of the entire National Institutes of Health budget – toward research on vaccines and autism, according to reporting by Reuters.

Decades of research into the causes of autism point overwhelmingly to genetics, and dozens of studies have indicated no link between vaccines and autism.

Even so, Trump issued an executive order in May urging HHS to change vaccine recommendations.

Kush Desai, a spokesperson for the White House, did not dispute the details reported by the Journal and others in a statement to the Guardian. He instead pointed to parents of autistic children – but not to autistic people themselves – with “questions and concerns” who “have long been ignored if not mocked”. The Trump administration was “committed to leaving no stone unturned” to address those concerns, Desai added.

Kennedy and Trump are “aligned in their commitment” to confront the “chronic disease epidemic affecting America’s children”, said Emily Hilliard, an HHS spokesperson, in an apparent reference to autism. HHS would “continue to pursue evidence-based research to identify the root causes of autism and other chronic diseases”, she added.

“I think Donald Trump has a fixed, immutable belief that vaccines cause autism,” Offit said. That makes Trump the most powerful anti-vaxxer in the world, Offit said – and it means he is unlikely to fire Kennedy, even as rumors have swirled that the health secretary is on his way out.

The abrupt rise of measles and other deadly diseases are more likely to be Trump’s legacy than advances in understanding autism, Offit said.

As top leaders have downplayed the safety and importance of vaccines, measles has surged to its highest rate in 30 years, and the nation has suffered a rise in deaths from whooping cough, flu and tetanus in recent years. “And our commander in chief, our vaccine guy in chief, is our president. He’s fine with this. Just as RFK Jr is fine with this,” Offit said.

“Trump has become the president of Measles Land,” Offit added. “That should bother him.”

articles.title: Democratic Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate doesn't recall 'abolish the Senate' post in 2021, campaign says
articles.excerpt: Fox News host Brian Kilmeade discusses the influence of democratic socialism within the Democratic Party after Democratic Socialists of America co-chair Megan Romer commented on the organization's pla...
articles.body_text:
Fox News host Brian Kilmeade discusses the influence of democratic socialism within the Democratic Party after Democratic Socialists of America co-chair Megan Romer commented on the organization's platform, which includes proposals to eliminate the U.S. Senate and abolish I.C.E.

Democratic Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong's campaign told Fox News Digital Tuesday that she does not recall posting on social media in favor of abolishing the Senate in 2021 and said that was not her current position.

Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) co-chair Megan Romer went viral Sunday for confirming that the DSA supported abolishing the Senate, eliminating national borders and prisons, replacing the presidency and the Supreme Court, and more during an interview with Shannon Bream on "Fox News Sunday."

Republican candidate for Wisconsin governor Tom Tiffany said in a post to X that Hong believed in all the ideas mentioned in the viral video.

"This sounds a lot like DSA-backed @FrancescaHongWI. Does she want to abolish the police? Yep. Does she want to abolish prisons? Absolutely. Did she call for abolishing the U.S. Senate? Yes. Socialism is knocking on Wisconsin’s door. This November, we slam it shut," Tiffany wrote.

DEM SOCIALIST RUNNING FOR WISCONSIN GOVERNOR PUSHED 'ABOLISHING THE POLICE'

Gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong speaks on stage during the Wisconsin Democrats Convention on June 14, 2026, in Madison. (Getty Images for WisDems)

When reached for comment, Hong's campaign said Tiffany was lying and said she never supported abolishing the Senate.

"Tom Tiffany is once again telling lies and inventing quotes, because he can't run on his record," Hong communications director Allison Geyer told Fox News Digital. "Rep. Hong has never called for abolishing the U.S. Senate. Tiffany cannot produce a single statement where she did, because it doesn't exist."

"She has spoken about police and prison abolition in the past as an aspirational goal, but it is not her current position, and it's not something she will pursue as governor," she continued. "She does not support replacing the presidency with the Supreme Court. Eliminating national borders isn't her position either, and it's not even part of the official DSA platform."

"DSA is a membership organization, not a political party. Rep. Hong is not endorsed by DSA national, and doesn't agree with everything in its national program," Geyer added.

MAMDANI-BACKED SOCIALIST IN HOT SEAT AGAIN OVER DELETED POSTS PRAISING COMMUNISM, MARXISM: 'CRAZYPANTS'

Tiffany's campaign pointed Fox News Digital to a post on social media from February 2021, in which she wrote on X, "Abolish the Senate."

Hong was responding to a post at the time highlighting Congress' vote to acquit President Donald Trump in an impeachment trial on the charge of inciting an insurrection for the Jan. 6 Capitol riot. A majority of senators found Trump guilty in a 57-43 vote, but the number fell 10 short of the supermajority needed to convict the president.

Hong's campaign told Fox News Digital that the gubernatorial candidate did not recall posting it.

WATCH: HOUSE DEMS DODGE QUESTIONS ON SOCIALIST AGENDA THAT THREATENS TO ABOLISH KEY INSTITUTIONS

Rep. Tom Tiffany speaks before Vice President JD Vance at the Wisconsin Air National Guard facility at Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport on July 8, 2026. (Mark Schiefelbein-Pool/Getty Images)

"The post is from February 13, 2021, the day the Senate acquitted Donald Trump for inciting January 6th," the campaign said. "She quote tweeted an analysis of that vote showing the senators who voted to convict represented roughly 70 percent of the country. It was a frustrated reaction to that day. It is not her current position, and it is not something a governor has any role in. She’s running to lower costs, fund public schools, and make childcare affordable."

The campaign said Hong has made her views on the matter very clear in recent interviews. Hong's campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for the specific interviews.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Francesca Hong, a Democratic state lawmaker and socialist candidate for governor, speaks to voters at a retirement home, July 7, 2026, in Madison, Wisconsin. (Scott Bauer/AP Photo)

Hong is not endorsed by the national chapter of the DSA, but her campaign website lists the Milwaukee, Northeast Wisconsin and Madison DSA chapters on her endorsement page.

Tiffany told Fox News Digital in a statement on Tuesday, "Democrat Socialist Francesca Hong can flip-flop all she wants, but she can’t hide who she is. She’s a card-carrying socialist who called to abolish the police, ICE, and even the U.S. Senate. Now her campaign is trying to rewrite her record because they know her ideas are too radical for Wisconsin, but they can’t rewrite her own words."

Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News.

articles.title: Zelenskyy and Netanyahu brave the whims of Trump’s darkly confounding White House
articles.excerpt:
Ukrainian and Israeli leaders converge on Washington with criss-crossing fortunes, but knowing they can count on little from US counterpart

The converging visits of Benjamin Netanyahu and Volodymyr Z...
articles.body_text:
Ukrainian and Israeli leaders converge on Washington with criss-crossing fortunes, but knowing they can count on little from US counterpart

The converging visits of Benjamin Netanyahu and Volodymyr Zelenskyy to Washington offer an unusually eloquent snapshot of a world in turmoil, unmoored from decades-old certainties.

Some things remain the same. The US is still an almighty military and economic power and for both foreign visitors, a White House encounter with Donald Trump is critical to their governments and the wars they are fighting.

The imperial presidency Trump has tried to forge is in decline, however, in large part as a result of his own erratic leadership. He may see his visitors as client-potentates flying in from the edges of empire to kiss his ring. But they will be as aware of Trump’s weaknesses as they are of their own.

Netanyahu and Zelenskyy arrive in Washington on opposite trajectories. The Israeli prime minister’s star has declined dramatically since he persuaded Trump to join him in an ill-conceived war on Iran five months ago, on the groundless promise that the Tehran regime would quickly collapse.

Since then, a viscerally disappointed president has publicly scolded Netanyahu and insisted Netanyahu would ultimately do his bidding, while the White House has liberally leaked Trump’s foul-mouthed tirades belittling him.

Israel has been left out of negotiations with Iran, and its views were ignored when it came to selling F-35 stealth fighter planes to Turkey, or making a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia. An Economist/YouGov survey found that nearly half of Americans polled thought that Netanyahu should be arrested on arrival for war crimes.

By contrast, Zelenskyy arrived in Washington in the ascendant. Ukraine has defied the US administration’s predictions of inevitable defeat to Russia’s might, his country is now a world leader in drone warfare, and parts of the Magaverse are now warming to the accidental war leader they once scorned as a loser.

In traditional administrations, both men and the countries they represent would be natural allies and both could be sure of solid welcome in the Oval Office. It is telling that the occasion of their coinciding visits was the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham, a Republican hawk of the old school who could be relied on for wholehearted promotion of the Israeli and Ukrainian war efforts. In that respect, he was one of a dying breed.

But this is no normal administration, led by a president who rules on a whim, and neither visitor can predict how he will be received. Neither wanted cameras in the room. Trump began his presidency by throwing all-in support behind Netanyahu and his wars, dropping even the pretence of concern for the lives of Palestinians or the people of southern Lebanon that had tempered backing for Israel from earlier presidents.

Facing a hostile electorate, the president is trying to extricate himself from the region, but in doing so is finding Israel the most recalcitrant party on every front.

In Ukraine, Trump threw out the American foreign policy handbook altogether, proposing peace deals that often echoed Moscow’s talking points, rewarding aggression with territory Russia had not even won on the battlefield.

Rather than capitulate, Ukraine showed it could fight on despite drastic cuts in US military aid, relying more on Europe and its own hard-won improvised expertise.

Now Zelenskyy finds himself the unlikely darling of far-right Maga influencers such as Lara Loomer, formerly an apologist for the Russian invasion, who interviewed the Ukrainian president in his garden last week, and called for “moral clarity” in Kyiv’s support.

Zelenskyy’s recent ascent may mirror Netanyahu’s simultaneous decline, but that does not mean they came to Washington with comparable status. When it comes to the Trump administration, they arrive from very different starting positions.

Just about anything would count as an upgrade for Zelenskyy compared with his infamous White House ambush in February 2025 by Trump and the vice-president, JD Vance, who tried to humiliate the Ukrainian visitor in front of the cameras, demanding gratitude and acceptance of defeat with “no cards” left to play.

Zelenskyy does have cards this time but well short of a winning hand without US support. The Ukrainian’s immediate aim is modest: for Trump to honour Senator Graham by backing a Russia sanctions bill he was pushing at the time of his death. He knows that direct US military aid to Ukraine is not likely to return in meaningful quantities any time soon.

The Patriot interceptors and other weapons Ukraine once counted on for its defence have been used up wholesale in the Middle East, many of them to protect Israel. It will take years for the US to rebuild its own stocks. Netanyahu may be out of favour in the current White House, but the US is committed to Israel’s defence in a manner and on a scale of which Ukraine can only dream.

Netanyahu and Zelenskyy came to Washington on different paths and footings but they do at least share an awareness that their relationship with the administration can be upended with scant notice, without any clear reasons, in a matter of mere seconds in the court of the irascible, flagging would-be emperor.

articles.title: Supreme Court denies stays for two Florida death row inmates, clearing path for rare double execution
articles.excerpt: The Justice Department is recommending the return of firing squads and other execution methods for federal inmates convicted of heinous crimes, fulfilling a President Donald Trump's campaign promise t...
articles.body_text:
The Justice Department is recommending the return of firing squads and other execution methods for federal inmates convicted of heinous crimes, fulfilling a President Donald Trump's campaign promise to prioritize victims over serious offenders.

The U.S. Supreme Court denied stays for two Florida death row inmates scheduled to be executed Tuesday, clearing the way for the state to execute the 11th and 12th inmates this year.

The court denied two separate requests for stays in the planned executions.

Former police officer James Duckett, 68, had been scheduled to die at noon on Tuesday, but the execution was delayed awaiting results of the stay requests before the Supreme Court.

THOMAS UNLOADS ON COURT FOR HELPING CONVICTED MURDERER BUT IGNORING 'LAW-ABIDING CITIZENS'

Duckett, according to local media reports, was executed by lethal injection and pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m.

Mugshot of James Duckett (Florida Department of Corrections)

Duckett was convicted of raping and murdering an 11-year-old girl in 1987.

The Supreme Court also denied a separate stay for Dominick Occhicone, an 80-year-old who was convicted of murdering his ex-girlfriend’s parents in 1986.

JUDGE BLOCKS ALABAMA'S NITROGEN GAS EXECUTION METHOD, RULES IT IS UNCONSTITUTIONALLY CRUEL

Occhicone's execution is scheduled for 6 p.m. If executed, he would become the oldest inmate executed in Florida.

Mugshot of Dominick Occhicone. (Florida Department of Corrections)

If carried out, Occhicone's execution would mark the first time Florida executed two inmates in one day since 1964. It would be just the second double execution in the U.S. in the 2000s and the first since Arkansas executed two inmates in 2007.

Clouds hover over the entrance of the Florida State Prison in Starke, Fla., Aug. 3, 2023. (AP)

Florida executed 19 inmates in 2025, according to a Fox News Digital review of Florida Department of Corrections data. The 11 people the state has executed so far this year are more than double the next closest state, with Texas having executed four inmates this year, according to the Texas Department of Criminal Justice.

articles.title: Iran expert brands Islamic Center of England Iran's 'UK office,' urges immediate closure
articles.excerpt:
Tousi TV founder Mahyar Tousi assesses Iran’s newly appointed supreme leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on ‘America Reports.’

A leading Iran expert has called on the British government to shut down a...
articles.body_text:
Tousi TV founder Mahyar Tousi assesses Iran’s newly appointed supreme leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on ‘America Reports.’

A leading Iran expert has called on the British government to shut down an Islamic center which he claimed has been functioning as an office of the regime’s supreme leader amid a shocking report that Iran’s regime smuggled operatives into the United Kingdom.

The Islamic Center of England recently came into the spotlight following revelations that the U.K. government has allegedly allowed the center to sponsor visas for imams. The report comes at a time when Iran has said Britain is a legitimate target if it allows the U.S. to use its bases to fly missions against Tehran.

The reported green light to imams to secure visas as "skilled workers" for the Islamic Center raises profound questions about dangerous gaps in Britain’s national security and immigration policies, according to lawmakers and Mideast experts.

UK PINS STRING OF ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS ON IRAN-LINKED GROUP, BANS IRGC

A Google maps photo showing The Islamic Center of England in London. (Google Maps)

Kasra Aarabi, Director of IRGC [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps] Research at United Against Nuclear Iran told Fox News Digital that, "In light of the IRGC’s threat to attack Britain and reports that it has been exploiting the illegal migrant crisis to send ‘Islamic revolutionary agents’ to the country, the U.K. government simply must not tolerate the existence of this Islamist extremist infrastructure on British soil."

Aarabi added that "The Islamic Centre of England — a U.K.-registered charity and mosque — has long been operating as the office of the Iranian regime’s supreme leader in the U.K.. Its Imam is the personally appointed U.K. representative of the regime’s supreme leader. The very fact that the supreme leader of the Iranian regime, who is ordering terror plots on British soil, has an office and appointed representative in the U.K. is completely unacceptable. In light of the IRGC’s latest threats against Britain, the center should be immediately shut down and all of its non-British staff deported."

The revelation about the Islamic Center of England comes amid a report in the U.K.'s Daily Telegraph that Tehran officials claimed that the IRGC controls some illegal human trafficking routes between the Middle East and the English Channel.

Firefighters are seen tackling a blaze at Highfield Road in the Golders Green neighborhood of London, following an arson attack on four charity ambulances belonging to the Jewish Community volunteer Ambulance Service. (PA/PA Images via Getty Images)

An Iranian official told The Telegraph, "Of course, don’t forget that our armed forces have influence and run the [smuggling] routes in some cases if they want." The official warned that "At the moment we have people right there in London, revolutionary people who care about the world and the lives of children – they wait for us to tell them what to do. We have not done that yet, but we can easily make London unsafe for you if we want to."

The official added, "These smuggling routes are more important and useful than the missiles for for us – we do not need a missile to target London, it’s easier than that."

WHO IS AHMAD VAHIDI? IRAN’S NEW IRGC CHIEF TIED TO GLOBAL ATTACKS AND ‘DEATH TO AMERICA’ IDEOLOGY

Fox News Digital previously reported in February that the Islamic Center of England was accused of selling merchandise supporting the U.S.-designated terrorist movement, Hezbollah and the IRGC — also a U.S.-classified terrorist entity.

The Islamic Center allegedly had stickers of late Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps global terrorist Qassem Soleimani, who was responsible for the murders of over 600 U.S. military personnel, according to the Trump administration. President Trump ordered a drone strike in January 2020 that killed Soleimani in Iraq.

A spokesperson for the United Kingdom’s Home Office — a  mix of the Department of Homeland Security and DOJ — told Fox News Digital, "The Islamic Center of England has not sponsored any workers since 2022 under the previous government, and the Charity Commission is currently investigating this organization."

Mojtaba Khamenei, the new supreme leader of Iran and second son of the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, attends a meeting in Tehran, Iran, on Oct. 13, 2024. (Hamed Jafarnejad/ISNA/WANA/Reuters)

The Home Office spokesperson continued, "We treat the threat posed by the Iranian regime and those who do its bidding with the utmost seriousness. That’s why we have fast-tracked a change in the law to outlaw support for the IRGC, equipping the police and intelligence service with more powers to disrupt those working on their behalf, and making it easier to prosecute them. If wrongdoing is uncovered, those responsible will face the full force of the law, with the possibility of lengthy prison sentences, loss of licenses, and further civil action."

Iran and its chief strategic ally, Hezbollah, have been blamed for bombing the U.S. Embassy in Beirut in 1983 in which 63 people, including 17 Americans, were murdered, and dual suicide truck bombers blew up the barracks of American and French members of a multinational force in Lebanon in 1983, in which 220 U.S. Marines, 18 U.S. Navy sailors and 3 U.S. Army soldiers lost their lives. Fifty-eight French troops were also murdered in the terrorist attack.

Critics have long urged the British government to pull the plug on the Islamic Center’s operation as pressure mounts on the new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, to act against Iranian regime apparatus in the country.

Aarabi said that "Burnham’s government should use all available tools — including the new designation of the IRGC under the National Security (State Threats) Act — to dismantle this Islamist extremist apparatus across Britain that is linked to the IRGC. To put it more clearly: all the charities, mosques and centers that have carried out IRGC-linked activity should be dismantled, and their non-British staff deported immediately. No ifs or buts."

He added "The Imam of the center, who is the representative of the Ayatollah in the U.K., has continuously expressed extremist views that are sympathetic to the IRGC. In spite of this, not only does he continue to reside in the U.K. but he is listed as the trustee of several charities in Britain. This individual does not hold a diplomatic passport, meaning his visa could be immediately revoked."

Naval units from Iran and Russia simulate the rescue of a hijacked vessel during joint drills at the Port of Bandar Abbas in Hormozgan, Iran, on Feb. 19, 2026. (Iranian Army/Handout/Anadolu via Getty Images)

US-SANCTIONED MOJTABA KHAMENEI NAMED IRAN’S NEXT SUPREME LEADER AFTER FATHER’S DEATH: REPORTS

Aarabi argued that the "IRGC has built an entire ‘soft power’ infrastructure across Britain under the guise of charities, mosques and colleges. The IRGC’s goal has been to use this infrastructure to nurture home-grown Islamist radicalization, terrorism and acts of violence. In doing so, it has successfully cultivated, within segments of the British Muslim community, what can only be described as an Islamist constituency that is loyal to it and its violent extremist ideology. These tactics mimic ISIS and al Qaeda — yet there has been no attempt to counter it by the British government."

Iranian agents have attacked Iranian dissidents over the years in Britain. Two Romanian nationals, who prosecutors said had been acting ​for Iran, were jailed this month for stabbing a journalist working for an independent Iranian news outlet Iran International in London.

Tehran has always denied involvement in such attacks, calling allegations ​to the contrary unfounded and politically motivated.

"If the IRGC seeks to attack Britain, it could activate this radicalized Islamist constituency for acts of home-grown violence and terror. This form of kind-actor terror, where a radicalized extremist carries out an attack because they’re ideologically inspired rather than paid or directed by Tehran, also provides the IRGC with sufficient plausible deniability to complicate attribution and reduce the likelihood of British retaliation," said Aarabi.

A protester waves a flag of the Islamic Republic of Iran during the demonstration in Millbank. Thousands of people marched to the U.S. embassy in protest against the U.S. and Israel's war against Iran. (Vuk Valcic/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

A spokesperson for the Islamic Center of England told Fox News Digital, "The Islamic Center of England is an independent registered charity, established and operating under the laws of England and Wales. It is governed by English charity law and regulated by the Charity Commission. It is not an official office or representative of any government, political entity, or individual."

The spokesperson for the Center added, "Like many charities, faith organizations and other eligible institutions in the U.K., the Center holds a Home Office sponsor license, which allows it to sponsor skilled workers where it meets the requirements of the U.K.'s immigration system."

The spokesperson concluded, "Sponsor licenses are granted and overseen by the Home Office, and all licensed sponsors are required to comply with the same legal and regulatory obligations. The Center has consistently maintained that it is an independent U.K. charity and carries out its activities in accordance with U.K. law and its charitable objectives."

The British Prime Minister’s press office referred Fox News Digital to the Home Office for comments.

Benjamin Weinthal reports on Israel, Iran, Syria, Turkey and Europe. You can follow Benjamin on Twitter @BenWeinthal, and email him at benjamin.weinthal@fox.com

articles.title: Acting DNI touts 'approximately 30% Staff Reduction from Weeks Ago' as Senate poised to confirm Trump nominee
articles.excerpt: Chad Pergram reports from Capitol Hill, highlighting Democrats pressing Clayton on his stance regarding 2020 election claims and his delayed testimony, a move orchestrated by President Donald Trump ov...
articles.body_text:
Chad Pergram reports from Capitol Hill, highlighting Democrats pressing Clayton on his stance regarding 2020 election claims and his delayed testimony, a move orchestrated by President Donald Trump over the SAVE America Act.

Acting Director of National Intelligence William Pulte has announced a fifth wave of office downsizing.

"Good News! In addition to the Historic DECLASSIFICATIONS (Transparency!) by the President, we are, this morning, Executing a 5th and Near Final Round of TERMINATIONS, an approximately 30% Staff Reduction from Weeks Ago," he wrote in a Tuesday post on X.

"The Intelligence Community must protect the American people, NOT the political whims of the bloated and corrupt elite class," he added.

ACTING DIRECTOR OF NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE ANNOUNCES 4TH WAVE OF LAYOFFS

Acting Director of National Intelligence Bill Pulte attends a kick-off celebration for the "Great American State Fair" on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., June 24, 2026. (Jemal COUNTESS / AFP via Getty Images)

Pulte on Sunday had announced the completion of a fourth batch of layoffs from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI).

"Since becoming Acting Director of National Intelligence, our team has been smartly, and carefully, reducing the size of ODNI, re-focusing ODNI on national security, the law, and the statute. As of this evening, we just finished a 4th round of thoughtful, measured layoffs. Thank you!" he declared in a Sunday night post on X.

In a July 10 post, he had stated, "U.S. National Intelligence is operating more efficiently and effectively than ever before, and today, we started a third round of reducing redundant, or non-critical, personnel. DNI’s future is exceptionally bright, and will be focused on following the law and the statute."

Pulte, the director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, took on the role of acting DNI last month as Tulsi Gabbard, who had been serving as DNI, departed the role due to her husband's cancer battle.

TRUMP'S DNI PICK JAY CLAYTON LOCKS HORNS WITH DEMOCRATIC SENATOR IN FIERY CONFIRMATION HEARING CLASH

Prior to when Pulte took the helm at ODNI last month, The Wall Street Journal reported that during an interview, President Donald Trump said he had informed Pulte that he thought the ODNI was "unnecessary and/or too big."

"I'd like to see it smaller. I think there are a lot of people in there that shouldn’t be there," the president said, pointing to Obama and Biden administration carryovers, according to the Journal. Asked if he was calling on Pulte to terminate workers, the president stated that he wanted Pulte to "start the process," noting that the eventual DNI nominee should carry on that effort, the outlet reported.

In part of a June Truth Social post, Trump declared, "I have named William Pulte to be Acting Director of National Intelligence, who will take over on June 19th, and have asked him to execute the immediate and needed downsizing of the office, reverting staff to their home agencies."

Fox News Digital reached out to ODNI on Tuesday asking for clarification on the reported 30% staffing reduction.

SENATE CLEARS WAY FOR TRUMP'S TOP SPY AS KEY ANTI-TERROR PROGRAM REMAINS IN LIMBO

United States attorney for the Southern District of New York Jay Clayton, nominee to be director of national intelligence, testifies during his confirmation hearing with the Senate Intelligence Committee at the Dirksen Senate Office Building in Washington, D.C., on July 15, 2026. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., said during a Senate floor speech last month that he had spoken with the acting DNI, who he says agreed "that we need to return the ODNI to its original size, scope, and mission by spinning off some of these functional... centers and sending intelligence officers who have been detailed there back to their home agencies so they can do actual intelligence work."

"He informed me that yes, a small handful of front office personnel are leaving federal employment, which is not at all uncommon when a senior leader leaves an agency or one comes into an agency," Cotton said. "He also said that a few dozen, around 45 or 50, career officers are, in fact, returning to their home agencies."

Trump last month announced that he was tapping U.S. District Attorney for the Southern District of New York Jay Clayton as his DNI nominee.

The Senate is slated to vote on confirming Clayton on Tuesday night.

Alex Nitzberg is a writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Several US schools to install pepper-spraying drones to respond to school shootings
articles.excerpt:
Company supplying drones said Ukraine-war inspired effort, where technique was effective in face of Russian attack

Several schools across the US are set to install pepper-spraying drones as part of a...
articles.body_text:
Company supplying drones said Ukraine-war inspired effort, where technique was effective in face of Russian attack

Several schools across the US are set to install pepper-spraying drones as part of a new effort to respond to school shooting attacks – a Ukraine war-inspired approach that is bound to put off those who would prefer leaders focus on preventing the violence in the first place.

Campus Guardian Angel of Austin, Texas, which describes itself as a response capability company, is providing the drones in question to multiple schools across the country, including at least four schools in Georgia, three in Florida and one in Colorado.

According to the company, which manufactures its own aircraft and firmware, the drones launch into action after an alert that a school is under attack and once its response team has confirmed the threat is credible.

They can be flown from thousands of miles away and support two-way communication through an embedded speakerphone, allowing the company’s response team to “engage verbally with a threat, or communicate to teachers and school staff”, Campus Guardian Angel’s website stated.

“This allows our team in our ops center to communicate to law enforcement officers verbally with messages such as ‘follow me and I’ll take you to the suspect’ or ‘open the door and we’ll go in to clear the room and tell you what we see,’” the company said.

The drones can remain airborne for around eight minutes on a single battery charge and operate at 900 MHz. According to the company, they can fly through windows that are not coated with ballistic film, using a front lance to break through. They are also equipped with sirens and can drop air poppers that create a loud bang.

Additionally, the drones carry a pepper launcher capable of firing pepper balls at a shooter and can also be used to deliver kinetic energy strikes against a confirmed attacker in an attempt to “greatly degrade or incapacitate” them.

The company said its goal is to “escalate the effects in waves of 3 or 4 drones, keeping the shooter occupied until he/she can be apprehended by authorized responders”.

Speaking to the Washington Post in an article published on Tuesday, the company’s co-founder Bill King, a former senior enlisted leader for Navy Seal teams with 32 years of experience, said: “Once I get the drones on you, you just can’t escape them.”

The company’s tactical operations director, Khristof Oborski, a former team leader with the Austin police department’s Special Weapons and Tactics (Swat) unit, added in another interview that the concept was inspired by the use of small drones on the battlefields in Ukraine after Russia invaded it in February 2022.

Speaking to Barron’s magazine, Oborski said King had observed the effectiveness of the technology during the war in Ukraine.

“He started thinking about how can you introduce this type of system to be able to combat a growing problem in the United States – with school shootings,” Oborski said.

The Georgia schools set to pilot the drone program include Coffee county high school in Douglas; Gainesville high school in Gainesville; River Ridge high school in Woodstock; and Statesboro high school in Statesboro. The state’s legislature included $550,000 in its annual budget to fund the program.

In Florida, Deltona high school in Volusia county is set to install 39 drones for the upcoming school year. Other schools expected to launch the program include Amos P Godby high school in Leon county and Boyd H Anderson high school in Broward county.

John Adams Academy in Douglas county, Colorado, is also preparing to introduce the technology. Speaking to Denver7, Sarah Kiesewetter, the John Adams Academy head, said: “We might be the first school in Colorado looking at [drone technology] but we certainly won’t be the last,” Axios reported.

However, not everyone is convinced the drones are the right approach.

That includes Tony Montalto, whose 14-year-old daughter Gina Montalto was among the 17 people killed in the 2018 mass shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas high school in Parkland, Florida. He told WPTV: “These drones aren’t patrolling – they just pop up when needed. So that’s part of the problem. We need to focus on the prevention piece rather than the reaction piece.”

Data published by the Washington Post in September show more than 398,000 students have experienced gun violence at school since the 1999 Columbine high school shooting in Colorado that killed 14 people.

articles.title: Thousands swarm stunning mountain escape as selfie tourism backlash erupts online
articles.excerpt: Viral video from Positano shows tourists packed onto a tight cliffside path with little room to move, drawing backlash online as experts say tour groups, day-trippers and social media are fueling over...
articles.body_text:
Viral video from Positano shows tourists packed onto a tight cliffside path with little room to move, drawing backlash online as experts say tour groups, day-trippers and social media are fueling overwhelming crowds.

The pursuit of the perfect selfie is creating headaches for one of the Italian Alps' most recognizable landmarks.

Viral videos shared online in recent weeks show massive crowds stretching through shuttle queues as visitors wait to reach Tre Cime di Lavaredo, one of the most iconic destinations in Italy's Dolomites.

The videos have sparked outrage, with many online commenters arguing that visitors were more interested in taking photos than enjoying the mountains.

FAMOUS BEACH NOW REQUIRES VISITORS TO RESERVE SPOTS WEEKS AHEAD AND PAY FEES

"This video proves that people are no longer able to enjoy the journey," one commenter wrote on Instagram. "In their minds, the only thing that matters is the photo."

"Everyone lined up for a photo just to show people on social media how great their lives are," said another user. "Hours in line for one picture."

Once-remote alpine destinations are now magnets for day-trippers and social media–driven tourism, bringing economic benefits but also crowded trails, parking chaos and damage to fragile ecosystems, according to many.  (Simone Padovan)

Tre Cime di Lavaredo is one of the most famous landmarks in the Dolomites. It draws visitors from around the world with its trio of mountain peaks.

The UNESCO-protected mountains are subject to the Enrosadira phenomenon, in which sunrise and sunset turn the rock walls a vibrant pink and orange, according to The Dolomites — UNESCO World Heritage Centre page.

Tre Cime di Lavaredo gets over 800,000 visitors per year, per the Tre Cime di Lavaredo Hike Guide.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Hikers and climbers gravitate to legendary vertical rock faces in summer, while winter transforms the region into a massive and interconnected ski network, according to Dolomites.com.

In response to the growing crowds, officials are considering requiring reservations for shuttle passengers in addition to the reservation system already in place for drivers.

Tre Cime di Lavaredo gets over 800,000 visitors per year, per the Tre Cime di Lavaredo Hike Guide. (Simone Padovan)

Drivers must reserve access to the Rifugio Auronzo parking area in advance, according to the reservation website.

Reservations cost €40 (about $45) for cars, €26 (about $30) for motorcycles and €60 (about $68) for camper vans.

Tre Cime is not the only destination in the Dolomites that's been grappling with issues caused by overtourism.

Landowners near Seceda, another popular mountain destination in the Dolomites, reinstated €5 (around $5.60) turnstiles to help manage growing crowds at one of the region's most photographed viewpoints, as Fox News Digital previously reported.

Videos have sparked criticism online, with many commenters arguing that visitors seem more interested in taking photos than enjoying the mountains. (Stefano Guidi/Getty Images)

Carlo Zanella, president of the Alto Adige Alpine Club, previously told Fox News Digital that the turnstiles were installed by a local farmer after visitors repeatedly trampled meadows while flocking to the scenic overlook.

Zanella also criticized the role of social media in reshaping mountain tourism.

"I am against the influencers," he said. "They are only interested in making money [through] advertising."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Zanella encouraged visitors to explore lesser-known areas of the Dolomites, saying there are "other even more beautiful places to visit."

Ashley DiMella of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

Kelly McGreal is a production assistant with the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.
